MIS Reporting

MIS Reporting localizations for California Community College clients.

The CCCCO MIS reporting system is a method by which institutions transmit unit record data on students, enrollment, schedules, and other institutional operations to the state regulatory agency. MIS extract processes draw data from Banner® tables and transform and format the data for submission as defined in the CCCCO MIS Data Element Dictionary.

CCCCO syntactical edits are not coded into the MIS reports. The reports' logic will not use the syntactical edits to replace user-added data. If a report hits syntactical errors during the CCCCO upload, the user must correct the data that caused the errors. (An example of this is CB report for elements CB21 related to CB03, CB04, CB05, and CB08.)

It is assumed that MIS report users are knowledgeable about the CCCCO MIS processes. Refer to the CCCCO for complete details on MIS reporting.

Note: At this time, CALBSTU MIS reporting does not support the use of baseline study path and baseline student centric periods. Both of these features update student data in ways that will not be reported by the MIS reports.

Setup scripts

If you did not implement MIS Reporting when it was released, be sure to run the following scripts when you do implement it.

Note: This does not apply to the AA, SY, and SL reports. For more details on these reports, refer to the MIS Reports section.
  • The mis_gtvsdax_resaddress.sql script inserts the RESADDR internal code into the GTVSDAX table and is needed for the SB_STU report. You will need to enter the RA address code when you run the script.

    This inserts the RA external code for the RESADDR internal code. This is used to identify which address type (RA in the example) for a student is to be used in MIS reporting.

  • The CALBSTU installation inserts GTVSDAX rows, which you use to define default values to be used for records that do not have respective data for elements SS01, SS02, SS03, SS04, SS05, SS12, SS13, SS14, SS15 defined on the MIS Success and Support Services Historical Data Page (SVAMSHD). See the Student Success Report (SS) design details topic for more information about these rows.
  • The CALBSTU installation inserts GTVSDAX rows with internal codes NFNVALUE and NLNVALUE. These rows define the values used to indicate that a person has no first name or no last name. These values are used to correctly report data for elements SB31 and SB32 in the SB_STU report.

    For example, if you use a period '.' in the first name field to indicate that a person has no first name, then you need to save a period '.' in the External code field on GTVSDAX for the NFNVALUE Internal code.

    Each row can only support one External code value, so you will need to ensure that all students with no first name all have the same value in the first name field as that recorded as an External code for NFNVALUE and all students with no last name have the same value in the last name field recorded as an External code for NLNVALUE or you will get incorrect values for SB31 and SB32.

  • For the CALBFA FA_FINAID report, there are two installed GTVSDAX internal codes of BOG0ACTUAL and BOG0CENSUS, which are installed with the default value of N (No). These entries control the printing of BOGW $0 awards on FA_FINAID report, which can affect whether the student ID is included on the SF_FINAID report, too. These GTVSDAX entries allow you to reflect whether your institution’s policies and procedures satisfy the strict CCCCO regulatory requirements for student attendance when reporting BOGW $0 awards. If you have any doubt or concerns and do not want to report BOGW $0 awards, leave these entries as N.

    These entries are also used by the SB_STU report. When CALBFA is installed, SB_STU calls the package created for FA_FINAID that uses these settings. If CALBFA is not installed yet, this package is skipped.

    The BOG0ACTUAL and BOG0CENSUS GTVSDAX codes work together as follows.
    • If both BOG0ACTUAL and BOG0CENSUS are set to anything other than Y (Yes) or if the entries do not exist, your FA_FINAID report will not list any $0 BOGW awards.
    • If only the BOG0ACTUAL entry is set to Y, any student that has a BOGW $0 award and attended at least one positive attendance class (attendance hours on SFAALST are greater than zero), the student’s BOGW $0 award will be included on the FA_FINAID report.
    • If only the BOG0CENSUS entry is set to Y, any student that has a BOGW $0 award and attended at least one census class with either a registered status or a drop status that has a registration date that is on or after the Calculated Section Start Date field on the Enrollment Details sub-tab of the Section Enrollment Information tab of SSASECT, the student’s BOGW $0 award will be included on the FA_FINAID report.
    • If both BOG0ACTUAL and BOG0CENSUS are set to Y, either attendance type (positive attendance or census) will qualify the student's BOGW $0 award to be included on FA_FINAID report.

      For multi-college districts, the attendance checking is based on each college’s registration data. Each CRN's campus code is linked to the GTVDICD codes on STVCAMP. The GTVDICD codes are used on all MIS report parameters. A student could have qualifying attendance in college A (that is, has qualifying registration data in one or more CRN with a campus code for college A), yet not for college B (that is, no registrations with the required data for any campus codes in college B). If the student’s $0 BOGW award is related to college A, it will be reported when the noted GTVSDAX entries are Y (yes). However, if the student’s $0 BOGW award is related to college B, it will not be reported regardless of the GTVSDAX settings.

MIS Reporting Tasks

Copy MIS report definitions

This section describes MIS report definitions.

About this task

Note: This task does not apply to the AA, SY, and SL reports. For more details on these reports, refer to the MIS Reports section.
Note: Because future releases will overwrite the delivered MIS report definitions, Ellucian recommends that you never modify these. Instead, use the Copy button on the Report Engine Validation Page (GVVRPDF) to copy a delivered definition, then use the copy for your own reports.

The following procedure explains the steps for copying an MIS report definition.

Procedure

  1. Open the Report Engine Validation Page (GVVRPDF).
  2. Select the report you want to copy.
  3. Click Copy.
  4. When the Copy Report Data to a New Report window appears, ensure that the code of the report you want to copy is displayed in the From Report field. If you selected the wrong report in step 2, you can change it here.
  5. Enter the code of the copy in the To Report field. This cannot be the code of an existing report.
  6. Select the Process Copy button.
  7. When the report is successfully copied, select the Return button to return to the main window.
  8. Modify the report definition to your requirements.
    For details, see REPT Banner General configure.
  9. Open the Report Engine SQL Page (GVARSQL).
  10. Enter the new report code in the Report field and then go to the next block.
  11. If the report uses an extract SELECT statement, change the REPORT_ID to name of your new report in the SQL Statement field.

    For example, if you copied the CC report and named the copy CC_LOCAL, when you open GVARSQL, the code would be a SELECT statement and you would find the following line of code:

    
SELECT 'CC' REPORT_ID,

    and change it to the following:

    
SELECT 'CC_LOCAL' REPORT_ID,
  12. If the report uses a PL/SQL block, continue as follows.

    For example, if you copied the SB_STU report and named the copy SB_LOCAL, you would find the following code in the SQL Statement field:

    
BEGIN
:sql_stmt_out := sv_mis_sb_stu.f_get_extract_sql
(:DISTRICT_COLLEGE_ID, :TERM);
END;
    1. Identify the extract SQL package (in this case sv_mis_sb_stu) and create a manual copy of the package and package body files with a new name, (for example, sv_mis_sb_local).
    2. In the new Extract SQL package, change the REPORT_NAME constant to use the name of the new report.

      For example, in this case you would find the following line of code:

      
REPORT_NAME    CONSTANT VARCHAR2(10) := 'SB_STU';

      and change it to the following:

      
REPORT_NAME    CONSTANT VARCHAR2(10) := 'SB_LOCAL';
    3. Adjust the functions and procedures of the new extract SQL package according to the requirements of the new report.
    4. Compile the new extract SQL package files with the BANINST1 user.
    5. Change the PL/SQL block code in the SQL Statement field to call the new Extract SQL package.

      Using the above example, the original code would be the following:

      

BEGIN
:sql_stmt_out := sv_mis_sb_stu.f_get_extract_sql
(:DISTRICT_COLLEGE_ID, :TERM);
END;

      and change it to the following:

      
BEGIN
:sql_stmt_out := sv_mis_sb_local.f_get_extract_sql
(:DISTRICT_COLLEGE_ID, :TERM);
END;
  13. Make any other necessary changes to the report definition to meet your requirements.

    For details, see REPT Banner General configure.

  14. Save your changes.

Assign permission to run a report

After a CALBSTU report is copied or a new report is created, users need security authorization configured to be able to run the report.

In addition, if you add new IDs for users who have MIS report responsibilities and need to use GVAREPT, they will also have to be set up with security permissions. For details, see Security setup in REPT Banner General configure.

Run MIS reports

The following procedure explains how to run MIS reports in the proper format for CCCCO submission using the Banner Report Engine (REPT).

Generating the reports through the Report Engine is a two-step process. You must first extract the data (the combined extract and transformation steps) using the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT). After the output exists, you must run the Report Engine Generate Report File (GVPRMIS) using the Process Submission Controls Page (GJAPCTL) to convert the data into a usable format that you can submit to the CCCCO.

For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

The following procedure explains the steps for running an MIS report through the Report Engine. For the run of a specific report, you do not need to run the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) extract and transformation step and the GVPRMIS step both at the same time; they can be performed hours or even days apart. See the note at the end of the procedure for more details.

Run the extract and transformation as follows

The following procedure explains how to run extract and transformation.

Procedure

  1. Run the desired report using GVAREPT.

    The parameters you enter in the Extract Parameter Values block are used by the extract to select the data to report.

  2. Take note of the sequence number displayed in the Run Sequence Number field.
  3. If the GVAREPT job completed successfully (that is, the status is Extract and transform steps completed successfully), continue with the next step to create the CCCCO submission file.
Create the MIS file for CCCCO submission

The following procedure explains how to create the MIS file for CCCCO submission.

Procedure

  1. Access the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS).

    If you access this process by selecting the Report Engine Generate Report File option on GVAREPT immediately following a successful transform, the system defaults the matching Parameter Set value.

  2. Run the process in the usual manner, noting the value you use in the Report Name parameter.

    This value is the name of the file submitted to the CCCCO. It will default to xx.ext , where xx represents the report name (such as CB for the CB report or SB_STU for the SB_STU report), which is in your job submission directory.

    After the GVPRMIS process completes, the .EXT file and the user-friendly .LIS file ( gvprmis_xxxxx.lis ) will be in your job submission directory. The .LIS file includes a list of the original parameters used on the GVAREPT extract.

  3. Review the .LIS file for accuracy.
  4. If any errors are found, correct them in the appropriate area of Banner, then repeat steps 1 through 3.
    Note: For a specific run of a report, you do not need to run the GVAREPT extract and transform job and the GVPRMIS stage both at the same time. You must have successfully run the extract and transformation stage before proceeding to the GVPRMIS step, but the stages can be performed hours or days apart. After the extract and transformation stage is completed, take note of the sequence number displayed in the Report Run Sequence field. When you are ready to run the next stage on GVPRMIS, enter that value into the Run Sequence Number field on GVAREPT for that stage. If you do not change the sequence value, the GVPRMIS stage will default to the data from the last successful run.

Set up security for SVAMISH and SVAMIST

These pages are used to enter each student's SG report data. A user can access the tabs on the MIS Special Historical Data Page (SVAMISH) and MIS Special Term Data Page (SVAMIST) only if their Banner ID is associated with the relevant business profile, as described in the following procedure.

  1. Access the FGAC Business Profile Assignments Page (GOAFBPR).
  2. Select the desired profile, as shown in the following table, in the Business Profile field.
    To allow access this tab... Select this profile...
    On SVAMISH
    Foster Youth SVAMISH_FOSTER
    Guardian Information SVAMISH_GUARDIAN
    Military SVAMISH_MILITARY
    On SVAMIST
    A2MEND SVAMIST_A2MEND
    AAHNPI SVAMIST_AAHNPI
    Career Advancement Academy SVAMIST_CAA
    CCAP SVAMIST_CCAP
    Foster Youth SVAMIST_FOSTER
    Justice SVAMIST_JUSTICE
    MCHS/ECHS SVAMIST_MCHS
    MESA/ASEM SVAMIST_MESA
    Puente SVAMIST_PUENTE
    SEA SVAMIST_SEA
    Student Work-based Learning Status SVAMIST_WORKBASED
    Transfer SVAMIST_TRANSFER
    Umoja SVAMIST_UMOJA
  3. Go to the next block.
  4. Insert a new record.
  5. Enter the Banner ID of the user(s) to whom you want to allow access to the selected SVAMISH or SVAMIST tab in the Fine-Grained Access User ID field.
  6. Save your changes.

Define institution controls on SVAIMIS

The following procedure explains how to define the MIS Reporting institution controls. These controls are used for the following reports.

About this task

  • College Calendar Day Report (CC)
  • Student Basic Data Report (SB_STU)
  • Special Population Data Report (SG)

These controls are defined by effective term ranges. If your institution’s offerings change, create a new record starting with the term of the change.

Procedure

Access the Institution MIS Control Page (SVAIMIS).
Special Population Data Report (SG) settings

The following procedure explains how to populate Data Report (SG) settings.

Procedure

  1. If your institution offers the Mathematics, Engineering, Science Achievement (MESA) program, check the MESA Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SG05 will list this program as Y (“not offered”) for all students reported on the SG report.

  2. If your institution offers the Puente program, check the Puente Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SG06 will list this program as Y (“not offered”) for all students reported on the SG report.

  3. If your institution offers the Middle College High School (MCHS) program or the Early College High School (ECHS) program, check the MCHS or ECHS Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SG07 will list this program as Y (“not offered”) for all students reported on the SG report.

  4. If your institution offers the Umoja program, check the Umoja Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SG08 will list this program as Y (“not offered”) for all students reported on the SG report.

  5. If your institution offers the Career Advancement Academy (CAA) program, check the Career Advancement Academy (CAA) Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SG10 will list this program as Y (“not offered”) for all students reported on the SG report.

  6. If your institution offers the Cooperating Agencies Foster Youth Educational Support (CAFYES) program, check the Cooperating Agencies Foster Youth Educational Support (CAFYES) Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SG11 will list this program as Y (“not offered”) for all students reported on the SG report.

Student Basic Data Report (SB_STU) settings

The following procedure explains student basic data report settings.

Procedure

  1. If your institution offers an apprenticeship program, check the Apprenticeship Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SB23 will list this program as Y (not offered) for all students reported on the SB_STU report.

  2. If your institution offers a transfer center program, check the Transfer Center Program check box.

    If you do not check this check box, element SB24 will list this program as Y (not offered) for all students reported on the SB_STU report.

College Calendar Day Report (CC) setting

The following step explains college calendar day report setting.

Procedure

If your institution offers a flexible calendar program, check the Flexible Calendar Program check box.

If you do not check this check box, element CC05 will list all calendar dates as Y (not offered) for all calendar dates reported on the CC report.

MIS mapping scripts and seed data

Set up your Report Engine Mapping Table (GVBTRMP) data using the optional scripts defined in this section after your first installation of CALBSTU. You can view and update these values in the Report Engine Map Values Page (GVATRMP).

About this task

After you have installed CALBSTU and run an optional script, you should re-run the script only if you have not modified or added additional data to the relevant table or to GVATRMP for the specific report associated with the script. For example, use the SD report scripts mis_sd_mapping_data_del.sql and mis_sd_mapping_data.sql only if you have not loaded any data for any SD element in GVBTRMP/ GVATRMP. If you have entered SD data, you should manually insert the SD data described in this section instead of using the scripts. The optional scripts discussed in this section populate GVBTRMP with the default or pseudo (that is, placeholder) data that will be used to convert your Banner values to the MIS-reported values, for example, converting address state codes into the numeric state MIS values.

In the Seed data tables, the value in the Banner Value column is a code you use in Banner, and the value in the Report Value is usually the equivalent MIS element reported value. In some unique cases, the value in the Report Value column is a code used only in the MIS report logic that helps map your Banner value to a specific location in the MIS report. For example, the SX report has elements that use the same Banner column, and the mapping links the specific values from that column to the correct element.

The delete script will delete ALL entries in GVBTRMP for the report, including the old default or pseudo entries and any entries that have been added by your institution. The insert script will insert the up-to-date default or pseudo entries.

After you run a script, you must review all the entries and replace the default or pseudo Banner values with your actual values.

After your initial CALBSTU install or upgrading to any releases, if the upgrade notes a change in one of these scripts for a defect or for an update from the CCCCO, you must take the following actions before running the script.

Procedure

  1. Access GVATRMP to review your existing entries to determine whether you have edited the GVBTRMP data.
  2. If you have not edited the GVBTRMP data, you can to run the respective delete and insert scripts and should not encounter any problems.
  3. If you have edited the GVBTRMP data, take one of the following actions:
    • Run only the insert script to add the new values.
    • Add the values specified for the relevant report manually using the Report Engine Map Values Page (GVATRMP).

Adult Education Assessment Report (AA)

Element AA02 ASSESSMENT-RESULT

This element indicates the result of the assessment. Mapping format for AA02 uses a valid 2-character value.

Use the AA02 seed data to map Placement codes to the appropriate AA02 value on SOAXREF with Electronic Label = STVTESC and Electronic Qualifier = AA02.

You can have multiple sorxref_edi_value values in the SORXREF table for a single report value. For example, if there are mutiple sorxref_edi_value values for the 'AA02' element in SORXREF like S11, S12, S13, S111, then only the first 2 characters will be reported for AA02, which is S1 in this case.

Course Data Report (CB)

Element CB27 COURSE-UPPER-DIVISION-STATUS

This element indicates whether a course is an approved upper division course associated with a baccalaureate program at the college.

Use the CB27 seed data to map STVCUDF codes to the appropriate CB27 value on SOAXREF with Electronic Label = STVCUDF and Electronic Qualifier = CB27.

Seed data for CB27

Banner Value Report Value Description
X A Course is an upper division course
X N Course is not an upper division course

In Banner, the Prior to College Level field on the baseline Banner Student page, Course Detail Information (SCADETL), is used to record the CB 27 element.

  • The Prior to College Level field is also used to print CB21, COURSE-PRIOR-TO-COLLEGE-LEVEL, which is an existing element that indicates course level status for English, writing, ESL, reading, and mathematics courses on the CB reports.
  • If the Prior to College Level value on the SCADETL page is not null and is any value between A-H, then CB21 equals the field value and CB27 = N.
  • If the Prior to College Level value on the SCADETL page is not null, is any value other than A-H, and if that STVCUDF value is mapped in SOAXREF to A for CB27, then CB27 =A and CB21 = Y. If the that STVCUDF value is not mapped, then CB27 = N and CB21 =Y.
  • If the Prior to College Level value on the SCADETL page is null, or the Supplemental Data record is absent on the SCADETL page for that course, then CB27 = N and CB21 =Y.

Student Pilot Programs Report (PP)

The delete script will delete all entries in GVBTRMP for the report, including the old default or pseudo entries and any entries that have been added by your institution.

The insert script will insert the up-to-date default or pseudo entries (if they do not already exist in your table by the primary keys).

Script Description
mis_sd_mapping_data_del.sql Deletes relevant GVBTRMP rows. Run this script before running the insert script.
mis_sd_mapping_data.sql Inserts new GVBTRMP rows for mapping to Element SD05 STUDENT-DISABILITY-DEPT-REHAB.

Element SB29 STUDENT-MULTI-ETHNICITY

The installation loads race codes (GORPRAC_RACE_CDE) for each SPAIDEN and other IDEN pages into the GVATRMP Banner Value field (GVBTRMP_MAP).

Note: If you have installed Banner HR and CALBHR, you should not change GVATRMP for SB29. CALBSTU MIS report SB_STU element SB29 uses the same application data as CALBHR MIS report EB element EB14 EMPLOYEE-MULTI-ETHNICITY. Setup scripts are provided with both product installations (if you have both products) to add the same validation data in the related tables. However, the EB report does not use the Banner Report Engine (REPT) and, therefore, has no mappings. If you alter the GVATRMP setups for SB29, you might create incompatible results between SB29 and EB14, and if the same ID is a student and an employee, SB29 and EB14 results might not match.

Additional values were added to the race code table (GORRACE) for SB38 STUDENT-EXPANDED-ETHNICITY and mapping rows were delivered to GVBTRMP to report the correct SB38 value for any given race code. At that time, additional rows were also delivered to GVBTRMP for SB29 so that the additional race codes would also map to the correct SB29 values.

Element SB40 STUDENT-EMAIL-ADDRESS

This element is used to report the student’s preferred email address.

Coding

  • If the email address contains fewer than 80 characters, left‑justify the value and pad the remaining space with blanks.
  • If the email address exceeds 80 characters, report only the first 80 characters.
  • If the email address is unknown, report the value as ‘X’ followed by 79 trailing blank spaces.
Note: Student must have a preferred and active email in Email information tab.

Added the SB40 element in Report engine, delivered as seed data.

Element SB38 STUDENT-EXPANDED-ETHNICITY

At 194 characters, the SB38 element is longer than the maximum character length that the GVPRMIS process can handle for a single data element.

Therefore, this element has been split into two parts – SB38A (100 characters) and SB38B (94 characters). This will have no impact on the file used for submission because the two pieces of SB38 will be seamlessly concatenated with no spaces or delimiters. The .lis file will have headings for SB38A and SB38B and the data will be across more than one row.

The installation loads each SPAIDEN and other IDEN pages’ race code (GORPRAC_RACE_CDE) into the GVATRMP CALBSTU Value field (GVBTRMP_MAP).

Mapping for positions 1 through 100 of SB38 will be recorded in GVATRMP for the SB38A data element, using report values of 01 through 100. Mapping for positions 101 through 194 of SB38 will be recorded in GVATRMP for the SB38B data element, using report values of 01 through 94. Position 101 of SB38 will be SB38B position 01, and so on.

The insert script will insert the up-to-date default or pseudo entries (if they do not already exist in your table by the primary keys).

Script Description
mis_sd_mapping_data_del.sql Deletes relevant GVBTRMP rows. Run this script before running the insert script.

Student Special Population Data Report (SG)

Element SG03 STUDENT-FOSTER-YOUTH-STATUS

The installation loads each SVAMISH foster youth status code into the GVATRMP Banner Value field (GVBTRMP_MAP). You must add your institutions SVVFYST Banner values to GVATRMP to translate them into the proper MIS values.

Note: The list of values installed in GVATRMP are from the original MIS SG report and use the original CCCApply values. Ellucian will not provide revisions through new scripts because you will need to maintain GVATRMP for SG03 based upon your list of SVVFYST codes.

Seed data

Banner Value Report Value Description
0 0 CCCApply: I have never been in Foster Care
1 1 CCCApply: Currently in foster care in California
2 1 CCCApply: Previous foster care in CA, aged out/emancipated
3 1 CCCApply: Currently in foster care in a system outside CA
4 1 CCCApply: Previous foster care non-CA, aged out/emancipated
5 1 CCCApply: Temporary foster care, did not age out/emancipate
Element SG22 STUDENT-A2MEND-STATUS

This element indicates whether the student met the educational criteria and received services from the African American Male Education Network and Development (A2MEND) program at the college during the reporting term.

Use the SG22 seed data to map A2MEND codes to the appropriate SG22 value on SVAMIST with Electronic Label = A2MEND and Electronic Qualifier = SG22.

Seed data for SG22

Banner Value Code Description
X 0 Not an A2MEND student
X 1 A2MEND student
X 2 A2MEND student with the declared intent to be a teacher
X 3 A2MEND student who withdrew from the program during the reporting term
X 4 A2MEND student who was dismissed from the program during the reporting term
X Y Not applicable, the community college does not have an A2MEND program
In Banner:
  • the MIS Special Term Data (SVAMIST) page is used to record the SG22 element
  • the Institution MIS Control (SVAIMIS) page is used to report if the A2MEND program is applicable for a term and district

The SG22 element is being reported on the Student Special Population Data (SG) reports.

If a code of Y is reported for this data element, all the records in the file must have a code of Y.

The data element cannot be self-reported; student participation in the program must be verified by the college.

The Social Economic Identity Rules (GOASEID) page is used to add the A2MEND values on the SVAMIST page. Each of the identity codes on GOASEID are created using the Social Economic Identity (GTVSEIR) report.

GTVSEIR- CALBSTUMIS is the code created on GTVSEIR for CAL MIS Reports and is used on the back-end to save data within the SVRPSID table, which is the new Banner Student baseline table created to save data for the SG22 and SG23 elements.

Element SG23 STUDENT-BASIC-NEEDS

This element indicates services or support that the student received through the Basic Needs Center at the college during the term.

Use the SG23 seed data to map SVR_TYPE codes to the appropriate SG23 value on SOAXREF with Electronic Label = SVR_TYPE and Electronic Qualifier = SG23.

Seed data for SG23

Position Meaning Coding
1 Food: student received services that enabled them to directly access food, food-related pubic benefits, and external food assistance programs like CalFresh

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
2 Housing: student received services for on-campus and off-campus housing support, navigation, placement, and referrals from the Basic Needs center or an external housing provider

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
3 Transportation: student received support for transportation to and from campus including the use of their personal car, parking, gas assistance, and public transportation

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
4 Mental Health: student received mental health intervention or prevention services including on-campus and off-campus services and referrals for counseling, therapy, peer support, and suicide prevention

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
5 Child Care: student received child care services including on-campus child care or family resources and referrals to external child care providers

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
6 Physical Health: student received on-campus and external healthcare including health-related public benefits and referrals to external health assistance programs such as MediCal/Covered California

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
7 Technology: student received support that enable a student to directly access the technology required to participate in and complete courses including assistance with a personal or loaner computer, WiFi, internet access, and on-campus technology resources

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown

0 = No

1 = Yes

X = Unknown
In Banner, the new Student Basic Needs (SVANEED) page is used to record the services delivered to the student. There is a tab for each of the following provided services:
  • Food
  • Housing
  • Transportation
  • Mental Health
  • Child Care
  • Physical Health
  • Technology
  • Veterans

The SG23 element is being reported on the Student Special Population Data (SG) reports.

The Social Economic Identity Rules (GOASEID) page is used to add the Service Codes on the SVANEED page. Each of the identity codes on GOASEID are created using the Social Economic Identity (GTVSEIR) report.

You must enter the Service Type in the Description field exactly to ensure it gets automatically populated on the reports.

GTVSEIR- CALBSTUMIS is the code created on GTVSEIR for CAL MIS Reports and is used on the back-end to save data within the SVRPSID table, which is the new Banner Student baseline table created to save data for the SG22 and SG23 elements.

Script Description
mis_sx_mapping_data_del.sql Deletes relevant GVBTRMP rows. Run this script before running the insert script.

Element SX04 ENROLLMENT-GRADE

The insert script loads each SFAALST grading mode code (SFRSTCR_GMOD_CODE) (grade mode selected during registration) into the GVATRMP Banner Value field (GVBTRMP_MAP).

This element is a special situation with a complex calculation. For this element, the values entered in GVATRMP are not used to translate normal grades into MIS equivalents. Anything that appears on the transcript and in Academic History, even if temporarily, will not use the GVATRMP conversion. Those grade codes must be directly entered into SHAGRDE and the student record, and will be directly reported on the SX report.

GVATRMP is used only for a situation where a gradable CRN does not yet (and might never) have a grade entered. The conversion takes the CRN's grade mode selected at registration (the Banner Value in the following table) and converts it into the appropriate CCCCO MIS code (the Report Value in the following table). These are the special CCCCO grade codes that are not real grades, are not loaded into the academic history, and do not appear on the transcript. Examples are noted in the seed data below.

Seed data

Banner Value Report Value Description
N UG Not graded; UG Ungraded Non-Credit
P UD Pass/No-Pass; UD Ungraded Dependent
S RD Standard; RD Report Delayed
Element SX06 ENROLLMENT-APPORTIONMENT-STATUS

The installation loads a default SSASECT attendance method for AB 955 designation (SSBSECT_ACCT_CODE) into the GVATRMP Banner Value field (GVBTRMP_MAP).

For this element, the value in the Report Value field (GVBTRMP_MAP_CHAR) links this entry to SX06 value 2 (AB955 Extension Section) and does not note the specific SX06 value to report. You should not load any value for the Report Value field other than AB-955. Replace the Banner value with your institution’s valid value(s) used as the SSASECT attendance method only for AB 955 reporting.

If for any reason the same class allows a mix of AB 955 enrollment and non-AB 955 enrollment, this must be done by a linked setup with two CRNs. The current design allows for AB 955 reporting without modifications to the database. This means the CRN is coded as being used for AB 955 through its SSASECT attendance method. Individual students are not designated as AB 955. Linking is the only way to allow for the reporting at the pilot colleges without intrusive changes to Banner. In other words, if the CRN has a special attendance method code (STVACCT) for AB 955 and that code is loaded into GVATRMP as an AB 955 code (the value in the Report Value field is AB-955 and the value in the Banner Value field is the CRN’s attendance method code), all appropriate students listed for the CRN will have SX06 value 2. If for any reason some students in the same class should not be listed with the SX06 value 2, you must use a linked class that has a normal attendance method to report the other students who do not have the AB 955 2 designation.

Student Vision Aligned Report (VR)

Element VR01 PROGRAM-IDENTIFIER

This element indicates the program providing the service received by the student.

Use the supplied SOAXREF seed data to map from either an Accounts Receivable TSADETC code or from a Financial Aid RTVARSC code to the MIS-VR program code. The values provided for VR01 will be used in conjunction with values provided for VR02 to identify the program/service combination for the code.

The codes for the VR01 fields are defined by the CCCO. In most cases, these codes can be associated with the Banner administrative page and tab where the data is maintained for a student. However, for the services that must be reported in dollars, we are allowing clients to specify for each relevant code both the program (VR01) and the service (VR02) that should be used in reporting. Please see Student Vision Aligned Report (VR) design details for more information about this specification.

For more information, see: Student Vision Aligned Report (VR).

Related reference
  • Student Vision Aligned Report (VR)
Element VR02 SERVICE-IDENTIFIER

This element indicates the service provided to the student.

For the services that are to report dollar amounts, use the supplied SOAXREF seed data to map from either an Accounts Receivable TSADETC code or from a Financial Aid RTVARSC code to the MIS-VR service code. The values provided for VR01 will be used in conjunction with values provided for VR02 to identify the program/service combination for the code.

The codes for the VR02 fields are defined by the CCCO. In most cases, these codes can be specified on the Banner administrative page and tab where the data is maintained for a student. However, for the services that must be reported in dollars, we are allowing clients to specify for each relevant code both the program (VR01) and the service (VR02) that should be used in reporting. For details, see Student Vision Aligned Report (VR) design details for more information about this specification.

In addition, the services that are to be reported in hours (D06 and D14) will only be reported from the SVACWSD page. If a student does have any of these hours from programs other than CalWorks, those entries will need to be entered manually to the output. In future releases, Ellucian will continue to refine these totals, with input from the client community.

For details, see Student Vision Aligned Report (VR).

Related reference
  • Student Vision Aligned Report (VR)

Seed data for XB12

Banner Value Report Value Description
X A Section has no associated instructional material
X B Section uses only no-cost open educational resources
X C Section has instructional material costs, but they are not passed onto students
X D Section has low instructional material costs (as defined locally)
X Y Section does not meet no-cost or low-cost instructional material criteria

In Banner, the baseline Banner Student page, Schedule Detail (SSADETL), is used to record the XB12 element.

Click LOV on the Degree Program Attributes tab on the SSADETL page to select the required attribute from the list.

  • If the attribute is mapped to a XB12 value on SOAXREF, then the attribute would be printed on the Section Data (XB) reports.
  • If more then one attribute is listed for a section and if both values are mapped to an XB12 value on SOAXREF, then you should select the attribute that occurs first alphabetically. For example, if an attribute maps to B and D, you should select B.
  • You can add the list of element values that are available on the Attributes field on the SSADETL page using the Attribute Validation (STVATTR) page.
  • You can map multiple attribute codes to each XB12 reporting value.

If an attribute is not mapped to the XB12 element, Y will be printed.

Element XB13 SECTION-INSTRUCTION-LANGUAGE

This element indicates the language of instruction of the section.

AB 1093 (2023) allows colleges to offer classes in languages other than English for non-English speakers without requiring the students to be enrolled in ESL. This element is not intended be used to denote foreign language instruction for English speakers.

MIS validation scripts and seed data

The scripts for the MIS Reporting functionality must be run with great caution. A pair of scripts is provided for each relevant validation table, one that deletes existing values and another that inserts new values.

Note: Before running a pair of scripts, carefully evaluate the existing values in the table. If you are using one of the codes to be replaced, you must make the necessary changes before running the scripts.

Only the values specified in the New seed data table below the script descriptions will be replaced. For example, if codes A, B, C, and D will be replaced by the script and you are using code X, too, code X will not be modified.

The script descriptions are arranged by report. Each script description section includes the scripts for the specified table and a chart of the new seed data that will be inserted when you run the scripts.

Some scripts apply to multiple reports, and in these cases, they are described in all report sections. This allows you to set up only the reports you want. Both reports are included in the script description so that if you have already run the script for one report, you will know you do not need to run it again.

MIS Reports

Adult Education Assessment Report (AA)

The Adult Education Assessment Report (AA) is a new annual file that will be reported every October for adult education assessments occurring in the previous academic year. The file contains one record for each distinct combination of college, student, assessment date, and assessment result.

Districts report information on adult education assessments administered during the previous academic year. The assessment dates (AA01) reported in the file should encompass the preceding academic year (July 1 - June 30). For example, report the Adult Education Assessment file with the term type of '220' with assessment dates of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The file with these records is submitted each October 1 for the previous academic year.

Use the SVRCAAA process to run the AA report. This report is not dependent on the REPT Engine (GVAREPT and GVPRMIS) used to run the existing MIS reports. Elements for the AA report are AA01 and AA02. (The element list is subject to change; check the CCCCO's data element dictionary (DED) for current values.)

The output file which is in .DAT format is used for final submission to CCCCO, and the file which is in .LIS format (user-friendly output) is used to evaluate results and troubleshoot errors/warnings in Banner as needed. After fixing the data issues, you can re-run the process to generate the .DAT file again before submitting to CCCCO.

The following criteria must be satisfied for a student's record to be reported in the AA report:
  • The Placement entries created for Adult Education Assessment on SOATEST is within the specified annual date range.
  • Campus entered in SOATEST matches the District code entered by user. (If there is no campus in SOATEST, then the campus provided in student’s curricula SORLCUR and general student SGASTDN is used.)
  • Each Placement code defined in STVTESC and used in SOATEST for recording the result of the adult education assessment is mapped to the appropriate AA02 value on SOAXREF.

For more details on seed data for AA, see Adult Education Assessment Report (AA) under the MIS mapping scripts and seed data section.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
Start Date Yes First date to be included in the report. This is the first day of the academic calendar (for example, July 1, 2006, for academic year 2007).  
End Date Yes Last date to be included in the report. This is the last day of the academic calendar (for example, June 30, 2007, for academic year 2007).  
District ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
UTF8 to Ascii Yes Determines whether Ascii conversion is required for data file.  

Course Data Report (CB)

The Course Data Report (CB) provides course information in the proper format as defined by the CCCCO.

Note: CCCCO syntactical edits are not coded into the MIS reports. The report's logic will not use the syntactical edits to replace user-added data. If a report hits syntactical errors during the CCCCO upload, the user should correct the data that caused the errors. (An example of this is CB report for elements CB21 related to CB03, CB04, CB05, and CB08.)

You can use the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) and the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS), as described in Run MIS reports, to run this report. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

Student Pilot Programs (PP) Report

The Student Pilot Programs report (PP) provides detailed information on student participation in pilot programs at the college during the reporting term.

Overview

The Student Pilot Programs report (PP) is defined for the California Community Colleges to provide detailed information on student participation in pilot programs at the college during the reporting term. Generate a Pilot Program record for each unique combination of college, student, and pilot program in which the student participated.

The file is submitted following the end of each term. Pilot program information is reported in the term the student participated.

For details on the official Student Pilot Programs Data Elements, see California Community Colleges Management Information System Data Element Dictionary.

Process

You can use the SVRCAPP process to run the PP report. The output file, which is in .DAT format, is used for final submission to the California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office (CCCCO). The user-friendly .LIS file is used to evaluate results and troubleshoot errors and warnings in Banner, as needed. After fixing any data issues, you can re-run the process to generate the .DAT file again before you submit to the CCCCO.

Parameters

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
District ID Yes District or College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be reported based on the STVCAMP setup. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
Term Code Yes Term for which data is being reported. Term Code Validation Page (STVTERM)
UTF8 to ASCII Yes Determines whether ASCII conversion is required for the data file.

The Student Assessment Data Report (SA) provides student assessment information in the proper format as defined by the CCCCO. It reports information on student assessment tests administered during the prior year.

You can use the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) and the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS), as described in Run MIS reports, to run this report. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

Student Basic Data Report (SB_STU)

The Student Basic Data Report (SB_STU) summarizes basic student data in the proper format as defined by the CCCCO. The CCCCO MIS report name is SB. SB_STU is the object name for CCCCO MIS SB report generated in CALBSTU.

July 2023 MIS Regulatory changes

As part of the MIS Regulatory changes delivered in July 2023, Ellucian added a new element, SB39/STUDENT-DEPENDENTS to the Student Basic Data report (SB report).

SB39 identifies the number of dependents supported by the student.

For more details, see the Guardian tab on the MIS Special Historical Data (SVAMISH) page in the Reference content and the 2023 MIS Regulatory Changes topic in the Release Notes content.

Overview

This report supports the FA_FINAID and SF_FINAID reports in CALBFA for Financial Aid MIS Reporting.

Note: CALBSTU MIS report SB_STU element SB29 also uses GVATRMP. If you have Banner HR and CALBHR installed, you should not change GVATRMP for SB29 because element SB29 uses the same application data as CALBHR MIS report EB element EB14 EMPLOYEE-MULTI-ETHNICITY. The EB report does not use the Banner Report Engine (REPT) and, therefore, has no mappings. If you alter the GVATRMP setups for SB29, you might create incompatible results between SB29 and EB14, and if the same ID is a student and an employee, SB29 and EB14 results might not match.

Additional values were added to the race code table (GORRACE) for SB38 STUDENT-EXPANDED-ETHNICITY and mapping rows were delivered to GVBTRMP to report the correct SB38 value for any given race code. At that time, additional rows were also delivered to GVBTRMP for SB29 so that the additional race codes would also map to the correct SB29 values.

Note: Before you use this report, you must access the Report Engine Map Values Page (GVATRMP) and update the related elements delivered values to those used by your institution. Elements for the SB_STU report are SB09 and SB22. The element list is subject to change; check the CCCCO data element dictionary (DED) for current values. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT).

SB_STU supports the SS report and includes the IDs that are included on SS only because of receiving services. These are IDs that are not listed on the SX report, such as an ID that received pre-enrollment services. To be included on SB_STU and SS, these IDs must be for a student record (on SGASTDN with a past, current, or future effective term) or an applicant (SAAADMS for a past, current, or future effective term) to provide the SB_STU element data. The order of priority for completing the SB_STU element data is as follows.

  1. If SGASTDN data exists that is effective for the reporting term (that is, the SGASTDN term is earlier than or the same as the report term), this data is used. (SGASTDN is term-effective.)
  2. If SAAADMS data exists that is effective for the reporting term (that is, the SAAADMS term is earlier than or the same as the report term), this data is used. (SAAADMS is term-specific. However, a prior term is used to populate the data that cannot be left as unknown or unreported.)
  3. If SGASTDN data exists that is effective for a future term (that is, the SGASTDN term is later than the report term), this data is used.
  4. If SAAADMS data exists that is for a future term (SAAADMS term is later than the report term), then use it.
    Note: If the ID is only an applicant without data in SGASTDN (that is, not a student), the transfer elements are set to their respective unknown values. Transfer data is calculated only for admitted students.

You can use the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) and the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS), as described in Run MIS reports, to run this report. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

July 2023 MIS Regulatory changes

As part of the MIS Regulatory changes delivered in July 2023, Ellucian has added the following elements:
  • SG24/STUDENT-DEPENDENTS that identifies if the student has been arrested, detained, or referred to probation as a youth and whether the student was detained during the reporting term
  • SG25/STUDENT-CAMPUS-HOUSING-STATUS that indicates whether or not the Housing program is offered by the institution
  • SG26/STUDENT-DUAL-ADMISSION-STATUS that indicates if the student is participating in a UC Dual Admission or the CSU Transfer Success Pathway Dual Admission program
In addition, Ellucian has removed the value 2 (The student is incarcerated in a California Youth Authority correctional facility) from the SG04/STUDENT-INCARCERATED-STATUS element.
For more details, see the following:
  • the Justice tab on the MIS Special Term Data (SVAMIST) page in the Reference content (SG24 only)
  • the Institution MIS Control (SVAIMIS) page in the Reference content (SG25 only)
  • 2023 MIS Regulatory Changes topic in the Release Notes content
