SG05 eligibility criteria clarification

This element indicates whether the student met the Mathematics, Engineering, and Science Achievement (MESA) program community college, educational, and financial indicators, and received MESA program services.

A student enrolled as an Achievement in a Science, Engineering, or Mathematics (ASEM) major must meet the following criteria:
  • have a declared Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) major
  • have a declared intent to transfer to a four-year institution
  • does not meet the MESA educational or financial indicators
  • received MESA program services

For community colleges that serve ASEM students, report the SG05 status using these codes:

Code Description
6 ASEM student
7 ASEM student with the declared intent to be a teacher
8

Pre-MESA or Pre-ASEM student (the student is recognized as a future MESA or ASEM student but did not meet the eligibility indicators at the time of application)

SSN Update Record Report (SI)

The SSN Update Record Report (SI) provides Social Security Number update information in the proper format as defined by the CCCCO. It lists MIS ID changes for both students and employees because employees can have similar ID changes in Banner, although less frequently than students.

You must enter the run date from the last CCCCO submitted SI Report, that is, the date the SI was run and its output submitted. These might be the same dates, but not necessarily. For example:
  • If the report was run in July but never submitted, the entered date would be the last submitted report run date (before July).
  • If the report was run on July 10 but not submitted to the CCCCO until July 12, the entered date would be July 10 to include any ID changes made between the 10th and 12th.

You can use the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) and the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS), as described in Run MIS reports, to run this report. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
District_College_ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup. This parameter is used only to update the GI01 entry. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
SI Last Run Date Yes Date on which the SI report was last run. If you cannot find the last MIS report run date, use the oldest date you believe it might have been because it is safer to over-report than under-report.  

Student Placement Data Report (SL)

The Student Placement (SL) file is a new annual file that will be reported each October for student placements occurring in the previous academic year. The file contains one record for each distinct combination of college, student, placement type, and placement date.

Districts report information on student placements in English, mathematics, and ESL occurring during the prior academic year. The actual placement dates (SL01) reported in the file should encompass the preceding academic year (July 1 – June 30). For example, report the Student Placement file with the term type of '220’ with placement dates of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The file with these records is submitted each October 1 for the previous academic year.

Use the SVRCASL process to run the SL report. This report is not dependent on the REPT Engine (GVAREPT and GVPRMIS) used to run the existing MIS reports. Elements for the SL report are SL01, SL02, SL03, SL04, SL05 and SL06. (The element list is subject to change; check the CCCCO's data element dictionary (DED) for current values.)

The output file which is in .DAT format is used for final submission to CCCCO, and the file which is in .LIS format (user-friendly output) is used to evaluate results and troubleshoot errors/warnings in Banner as needed. After fixing the data issues, you can re-run the process to generate the .DAT file again before submitting to CCCCO.

The following criteria must be satisfied for a student's record to be reported in the SL report:
  • The Placement entries created for Student Placement Data Reporting on SOATEST is within the specified annual date range.
  • Test Code has a single-character MIS code in STVTESC and that single-character MIS code is one of the valid values for SL02 Placement Type.
  • Campus entered in SOATEST matches the District code entered by user. (If there is no campus in SOATEST, then the campus provided in student’s curricula SORLCUR and general student SGASTDN is used.)
Note: For an element mapping in the SORXREF table, ensure that you do not map the same Banner value to more than one report value.

For example, for SL03 mapping, if 'CLT1' (Banner value) is mapped to the report value 'A' and also 'B', then it will cause issues while running the report.

For details on seed data for SL, see Student Placement Report (SL) under the MIS mapping scripts and seed data section.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
Start Date Yes First date to be included in the report. This is the first day of the academic calendar (for example, July 1, 2006, for academic year 2007).  
End Date Yes Last date to be included in the report. This is the last day of the academic calendar (for example, June 30, 2007, for academic year 2007).  
District College ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
UTF8 to Ascii Yes Determines whether Ascii conversion is required for data file.  

Student Nursing Report (SN)

The Student Nursing report (SN) is defined for the California Community Colleges to provide detailed information on nursing students and applicants. It is based on the academic year.

Report student participation in a nursing program at the college for the specified reporting term. Generate a Student Nursing record for each unique combination of college, student, and nursing program in which the student is enrolled.

This file is submitted annually each September for the previous academic year. Nursing program participation is reported for the academic year in which the student participates.

Use the SVRCASN process to run the SN report.

The output file, which is in .DAT format, is used for final submission to California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office (CCCCO), and the file, which is in a user-friendly .LIS format, is used to evaluate results and troubleshoot errors and warnings in Banner as needed. After fixing the data issues, you can re-run the process to generate the .DAT file again before submitting to CCCCO.

For details on the official Student Nursing Data Elements, see California Community Colleges Management Information System Data Element Dictionary.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
Academic Year No Code of the academic year. This can be any valid value from STVACYR except 0000 and 9999. Academic Year Validation Page (STVACYR)
District ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
Student ID Yes Student ID  
UTF8 to ASCII Yes Determines whether ASCII conversion is required for the data file  
Note: Some of the fields in the file are used in multiple files or reports; some are unique to this file. Those files that are unique are identified with a prefix of SN concatenated with the DED number.

This process uses the SVVNRUP (Nursing Program) view to read the nursing programs for a student.

Table 1. TOPS codes for nursing programs
Code Program
1230.00 Nursing
1230.10 Registered Nursing
1230.20 Licensed Vocational Nursing
1230.30 Certified Nurse Assistant
1230.80 Home Health Aide

Before you begin: Prerequisites and configuration sequence

Complete the following configuration steps in order before running SVRCASN. Running SVRCASN before crosswalk configuration is complete produces silently incorrect output. Fields that depend on missing crosswalk entries are blank or X with no warning in the .LIS file.

  1. Configure SOAXREF crosswalks for all required MIS-SN elements:
    • NURSPROG crosswalk for SP04. See Configure the NURSPROG crosswalk for SP04.
    • STVTESC crosswalk for SN02 (TEAS). See Configure TEAS test scores for SN02.
    • STVTESC and NURSCORE crosswalks for SN03 and SN04 (NCLEX). See Configure NCLEX test scores for SN03 and SN04.
    • STVLANG crosswalk for SN05. See Configure language proficiency codes for SN05.
  2. Enter nursing program enrollment data for each student on the MIS Special Academic Year Data (SVAMISA) page.
  3. Run SVRCASN.
Warning: If SVRCASN is run before the crosswalk configuration is complete, the affected SN output fields contain blank or X values without any error message in the .LIS file. Re-running SVRCASN after completing configuration corrects the output.

Run SVRCASN

Note: If institutions are part of a multi-institution district, each individual institution must run SVRCASN separately using their own District/College ID (DCID).

Use the SVRCASN process to generate the Student Nursing (SN) report. The process produces:

  • A .DAT file for final submission to CCCCO.
  • A .LIS file for reviewing results and troubleshooting data issues before submission.

After reviewing the .LIS file and correcting any data issues, re-run SVRCASN to generate an updated .DAT file before submitting to CCCCO.

Common problems and possible solutions

  • A valid SN program is not recognized.
    • The field in the file for the students is left blank.
    • There is an error message in the .LIS file.
    • Check the SOAXREF entry for NURSPROG to be sure the program code matches the SMAPRLE entry.
    • Check that the case matches between the two sources. For example, SOAXREF displays Nursing as NURSING.
    • If necessary, retype the SOAXREF Banner value in upper case, Save, and then try rerunning the report.
  • Valid TEAS scores are triggering an error message.
    • This is a known problem with the error message which will be corrected in a future release.
    • The data in the file is correct.
  • SN03 shows Y (did not take NCLEX) for students who took NCLEX.
    • Verify that the student has a SORTEST record for the NCLEX test code within the applicable academic year date range.
    • Verify that the STVTESC code for the student matches the Banner Value in the SOAXREF SN03 entry (Label = STVTESC, Qualifier = SN03DCID).
    • Verify that a NURSCORE SOAXREF entry exists for the local score code for the student.
  • SN05 shows all X characters for most or all students.
    • Verify that students have SORLANP records on the Language Proficiency Details page (SOALANP).
    • Verify that SOAXREF STVLANG entries exist with Qualifier = SN05 for each language code used at the institution.
    • Verify that LANGPROF seed data is loaded in SOAXREF.
  • Output fields are blank for all students at a specific campus.

    Verify that all SOAXREF qualifier codes for NURSPROG, SN02, SN03, NURSCORE, and SN05 use the same District/College ID as the District ID job parameter for the SVRCASN run. See the individual configuration topics for each element.

For more information, visit the official California Community Colleges Chancellor’s Office page.

Configure the NURSPROG crosswalk for SP04

Before running SVRCASN, configure the NURSPROG crosswalk in SOAXREF to map institution-specific nursing program codes to the SP04 element values required for the CCCCO MIS-SN report.

Overview

The NURSPROG crosswalk in SOAXREF serves two purposes:

  • It populates the Program Name list of values (LOV) on the SVAMISA Nursing tab. This allows users to select the applicable nursing program when recording student data.
  • It maps the selected program code to the CCCCO SP04 MIS element value used by SVRCASN when it generates the SN report.

Each SOAXREF entry for NURSPROG maps one institution-specific program code from the Program Definition Rules (SMAPRLE) page to its corresponding SP04 EDI value.

Prerequisites

  • Define nursing program codes in the Program Definition Rules (SMAPRLE) page with a CO-Unique code populated. The CO-Unique code is the value entered as the Banner Value in the SOAXREF NURSPROG entry.
  • The NURSPROG label exists in the Cross-Reference Label Validation (STVXLBL) page before you create SOAXREF entries. See STVXLBL.

SOAXREF entry format for NURSPROG

On the Cross-Reference Rules (SOAXREF) page, create one entry for each nursing program code using the following values:

SOAXREF Field Value Notes
Label NURSPROG Matches the STVXLBL code exactly, including case.
Qualifier SP04DCID Replace DCID with the District/College ID (GI01 value) used in the SVRCASN District ID job parameter. For example, if DCID = 123, enter SP04123.
Banner Value program-code

The CO-Unique code from SMAPRLE for the nursing program. This value matches the SMAPRLE entry exactly, including case. SOAXREF is case-sensitive.
EDI Value SP04-value The CCCCO SP04 element value that this program maps to. Refer to the CCCCO MIS Data Element Dictionary for valid SP04 values.

Common problems and possible solutions

  • Program Name LOV is empty on SVAMISA Nursing tab.

    No SOAXREF NURSPROG entries exist with the qualifier matching the District/College ID. Verify that all SOAXREF NURSPROG entries use the qualifier format SP04DCID where DCID matches the District/College ID. Create missing entries.

  • SP04 is blank in the SN output for specific students.

    The program code recorded on SVAMISA does not match the Banner Value in the SOAXREF entry. Check the case as SOAXREF is case-sensitive. For example, Nursing and NURSING are treated as different values. Retype the Banner Value in the correct case, save, and re-run SVRCASN.

  • SP04 is blank for all students at a specific campus.

    Verify that the SOAXREF qualifier for each NURSPROG entry uses the correct District/College ID value, exactly matching the District ID parameter used in the SVRCASN job.

Configure TEAS test scores for SN02

Configure STVTESC and SOAXREF to enable SVRCASN to identify ATI TEAS test records and derive the SN02 (TEAS score) element in the Student Nursing report.

Overview

The SN02 element reports the ATI TEAS (Test of Essential Academic Skills) score result for the student. SVRCASN derives SN02 by locating SORTEST records for the academic year that match STVTESC codes configured with the required test type indicator for TEAS, then mapping the score to the SN02 EDI value through the SOAXREF crosswalk.

Prerequisites

  • Define TEAS test codes on the Test Score Code Validation (STVTESC) page with the appropriate test type indicator designating them as MIS-SN TEAS records.
  • The STVTESC label exists in STVXLBL before you create SOAXREF entries. See STVXLBL.
  • Record student TEAS scores in SORTEST using your STVTESC codes, within the applicable academic year date range.

Step 1: Configure the STVTESC test type for TEAS

On the Test Score Code Validation (STVTESC) page, verify or update the test type indicator for each TEAS test code used at the institution.

Step 2: Configure the SN02 crosswalk in SOAXREF

On the Cross-Reference Rules (SOAXREF) page, create one entry per TEAS test code using the following values:

SOAXREF Field Value Notes
Label STVTESC Matches the STVXLBL code exactly.
Qualifier SN02DCID Replace DCID with the District/College ID. For example, if DCID = 123, enter SN02123.
Banner Value TEAS-test-code

The STVTESC code for the TEAS test as recorded in SORTEST. Create one SOAXREF entry for each TEAS test code used at the institution.
EDI Value SN02-value The CCCCO SN02 element value for this test score mapping. Refer to the CCCCO MIS Data Element Dictionary for valid SN02 values.

Common problems and possible solutions

  • Valid TEAS scores are triggering an error message in the .LIS file.

    This is a known issue with the error message. The error message is corrected in a future release. The data in the SN output file is correct. You can proceed with submission.

  • SN02 is blank for students with TEAS scores.

    Verify that a SOAXREF entry exists for the TEAS test code for the student with the Label = STVTESC and Qualifier = SN02DCID. Verify that the Banner Value matches the STVTESC code recorded in the SORTEST record for the student exactly, including case.

  • SN02 is blank for all students at a specific campus.

    Verify that the qualifier in each SOAXREF SN02 entry matches the District/College ID used in the SVRCASN job parameter exactly.

Configure NCLEX test scores for SN03 and SN04

Configure STVTESC and SOAXREF to enable SVRCASN to identify NCLEX test records and derive the SN03 (NCLEX attempt status) and SN04 (NCLEX date) elements in the Student Nursing report.

Overview

The SN03 element reports the NCLEX (National Council Licensure Examination) attempt status for the student. The SN04 element reports the date the student took the NCLEX exam. SVRCASN derives these elements by locating SORTEST records that match STVTESC codes configured as NCLEX tests, and then mapping the result through the NURSCORE crosswalk.

SN03 values are derived using the following logic:

  • If the student has an NCLEX SORTEST record with a score code matching a NURSCORE SOAXREF entry, the mapped CCCCO value is used (A = passed, B = failed).
  • If the student has an NCLEX record but no matching NURSCORE entry, SN03 = C (took exam, result not available for reporting).
  • If the student has no qualifying NCLEX SORTEST record for the academic year date range, SN03 = X (not applicable).
  • If the student is expected to have taken NCLEX but the qualifying record cannot be matched to the crosswalk, SN03 = Y (did not take).

Prerequisites

  • Define NCLEX test codes on the Test Score Code Validation (STVTESC) page with the appropriate test type indicator designating them as NCLEX records for MIS-SN.
  • The STVTESC label exists in STVXLBL before you create SOAXREF entries. See STVXLBL.
  • Record student NCLEX scores in SORTEST using your STVTESC NCLEX codes and local pass/fail score codes, within the applicable academic year date range.
  • Identify institution-specific NCLEX score codes (pass/fail indicators stored in SORTEST) before creating NURSCORE SOAXREF entries.

Step 1: Configure the STVTESC test type for NCLEX

On the Test Score Code Validation (STVTESC) page, verify or update the test type indicator for each NCLEX test code used at the institution.

Step 2: Configure the SN03 crosswalk in SOAXREF

On the Cross-Reference Rules (SOAXREF) page, create one entry per NCLEX test code identifying it as an NCLEX qualifying test:

SOAXREF Field Value Notes
Label STVTESC  
Qualifier SN03DCID Replace DCID with the District/College ID. For example, if DCID = 123, enter SN03123.
Banner Value NCLEX-test-code The STVTESC code used when recording NCLEX scores in SORTEST.
EDI Value SN03-qualifier-value The CCCCO SN03 qualifier value. Refer to the CCCCO MIS Data Element Dictionary for valid values.

Step 3: Configure the NURSCORE crosswalk in SOAXREF

The NURSCORE crosswalk maps local NCLEX pass/fail score codes stored in SORTEST to the CCCCO SN03 status values (A = passed, B = failed). Create one entry per local score code:

SOAXREF Field Value Notes
Label NURSCORE  
Qualifier SN03DCID Matches the SN03 qualifier used in Step 2.
Banner Value local-score-code The institution-specific NCLEX pass/fail score code as stored in SORTEST. These values are not delivered as seed data. Enter these values based on the local SORTEST configuration.
EDI Value A or B A = passed NCLEX; B = failed NCLEX. Refer to the CCCCO MIS Data Element Dictionary for the authoritative SN03 value definitions.

Common problems and possible solutions

  • SN03 shows Y (did not take NCLEX) for students who took NCLEX.

    Check the following in order:

    1. Verify that the student has a SORTEST record for the NCLEX test code within the applicable academic year date range.
    2. Verify that the STVTESC code in the SORTEST record for the student matches the Banner Value in the SOAXREF SN03 entry (Label = STVTESC, Qualifier = SN03DCID).
    3. Verify that a NURSCORE SOAXREF entry exists for the local score code for the student (Label = NURSCORE, Qualifier = SN03DCID).
  • SN03 and SN04 are blank for all students at a campus.

    Verify that all SOAXREF SN03 and NURSCORE qualifier values use the correct District/College ID, matching the District ID parameter used in the SVRCASN job.

Configure language proficiency codes for SN05

Configure SOAXREF to map institution-specific language codes from SORLANP to the 15-position SN05 (language proficiency) element derived by SVRCASN in the Student Nursing report.

Overview

The SN05 element is a 15-character string in the SN output file. Each character position corresponds to a specific language, and the value for each position indicates whether the student has recorded language proficiency data for that language:

  • Y = student has a proficiency record for this language in SORLANP
  • N = student does not have proficiency data for this language
  • X = not reported (no SORLANP data, or crosswalk mapping not found)

SVRCASN derives each SN05 position by checking whether the student has a SORLANP record matching the STVLANG code mapped to that position in SOAXREF, then applying the LANGPROF seed data determination rules.

CAUTION:
If SORLANP records exist for students but the STVLANG crosswalk entries are missing or incomplete, SVRCASN writes X for each affected position for all students — potentially resulting in all fifteen characters being X for the entire submission. Complete the STVLANG crosswalk configuration before running SVRCASN.

Prerequisites

  • Record student language proficiency data in SORLANP, accessible through the Language Proficiency Details page (SOALANP).
  • The LANGPROF seed data is loaded in SOAXREF. LANGPROF is a delivered crosswalk used internally by SVRCASN for SN05 derivation logic. Do not modify LANGPROF entries.
  • Your STVLANG language codes are identified before you create SOAXREF STVLANG crosswalk entries for SN05.

SN05 language position reference

The following table shows the 15 SN05 positions, the corresponding language name, and the CCCCO identifier.

Position Language (CCCCO identifier)
1 American Sign Language (S0101)
2 Spanish (S0201)
3 Chinese (S0301)
4 Tagalog (S0401)
5 Vietnamese (S0501)
6 Korean (S0601)
7 Japanese (S0701)
8 German (S0801)
9 Farsi/Persian (S0901)
10 Armenian (S1001)
11 French (S1101)
12 Russian (S1201)
13 Arabic (S1301)
14 Languages of India (Bengali, Hindi, Punjabi, and so on) (S1401)
15 Languages of the African continent (S1501)

Configure the STVLANG crosswalk in SOAXREF

On the Cross-Reference Rules (SOAXREF) page, create one entry for each language code for each of the 15 SN05 positions:

SOAXREF Field Value Notes
Label STVLANG  
Qualifier SN05 All 15 language entries use the same qualifier.
Banner Value institution-language-code The STVLANG code as stored in the SORLANP record for the student. These are defined by each institution. The Banner Value matches the STVLANG code in SORLANP exactly, including case.
EDI Value S-position-identifier The CCCCO SN05 language identifier for the corresponding position (for example, S0101 for ASL, S0201 for Spanish). See the SN05 language position reference table above.
Warning: Do not modify LANGPROF entries in SOAXREF. LANGPROF is seed data delivered with this release and is used internally by SVRCASN for SN05 derivation logic. Modifying LANGPROF entries causes incorrect SN05 output.

Common problems and possible solutions

  • SN05 shows all X characters (fifteen X) for most or all students.

    Check the following in order:

    1. Verify that students have SORLANP records on the Language Proficiency Details (SOALANP) page for the applicable academic year.
    2. Verify that SOAXREF entries exist with Label = STVLANG and Qualifier = SN05 for each language code used at the institution.
    3. Verify that the LANGPROF seed data is loaded in SOAXREF. If the LANGPROF entries are missing, contact your Banner support team.
  • Position 15 (S1501, languages of the African continent) shows X for all students.

    Verify that a SOAXREF entry exists with Label = STVLANG, Qualifier = SN05, and EDI Value = S1501, and that the Banner Value matches the STVLANG code for this language group. If the entry is missing, add it manually or contact your Banner support team to confirm whether a seed data script is available.

Student Program Award Data Report (SP)

The Student Program Award Data Report (SP) provides student program award information in the proper format as defined by the CCCCO.

Note: Before you use this report, you must access the Report Engine Map Values Page (GVATRMP) and update the related element’s delivered values to those used by your institution. The element for the SP report is SP02. (The element list is subject to change; check the CCCCO's data element dictionary (DED) for current values.)

You can use the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) and the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS), as described in Run MIS reports, to run this report. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
Start Date Yes First date to be included in the report. This is the first day of the academic calendar (for example, July 1, 2006, for academic year 2007).  
End Date Yes Last date to be included in the report. This is the last day of the academic calendar (for example, June 30, 2007, for academic year 2007).  
District_College_ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)

Student Success Report (SS) for MIS

The Student Success Report (SS) provides student success information in the proper format as defined by the CCCCO.

The CCCCO requires that every ID listed on the MIS SS report for a term must also be listed on CCCCO MIS SB for that term. In CALBSTU, only SB_STU has this domain or record selection relationship.

For more details about the design of this report, see Student Success Report (SS) design details section.

You must also update the MIS Student Success Term Enrollment Absence Rules Page (SVRTMIS) for the calculations of some elements. Refer How SS element values are calculated for more information.

Note: Before you use this report, you must access the Report Engine Map Values Page (GVATRMP) and update the related elements' delivered values to those used by your institution. The element for the SS report is SS01. The element list is subject to change; check the CCCCO data element dictionary (DED) for current values.

You can use the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) and the Report Engine Process (GVPRMIS), as described in Run MIS reports, to run this report. For details, Report Engine Run (GVAREPT) documentation for details about GVPRMIS and information about how to create a modified report.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
District_College_ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
Term Yes Term for which data is being reported Term Code Validation Page (STVTERM)
Student Success Report (SS) design details

The CCCCO requirements for the SS report are complex, so the design of the CALBSTU MIS SS report is substantially different from other MIS reports. This section provides details about the design and workings of this report for credit and noncredit service and supporting data reporting.

The information in this section is provided to help you understand the SS report, the design decisions behind it, and its output results. It is to help you plan and prepare for your SS report. As one example, the calculations area is a guideline to understand how the results on SS are achieved. The logic for this report is much more intricate than for other MIS reports.

As detailed in this section, the MIS Success and Support Services Term Data Page (SVAMSTD) provides a preview to the SS report output for the elements maintain on that page. This is accomplished by using the same package and procedure that the SS report uses. Therefore, if you modify the SS report and make a local copy (for example, SS_LOCAL), you should review SVAMSTD. For accuracy in the preview block, you might need to change the calling procedure ( sv_mis_ss.f_get_extract_sql ).

The documentation of the MIS SS report uses terminology, such as three-year absence and initial, with specific meanings to the California Community Colleges. Refer to the CCCCO regulations for clarifications on all topics and definitions.

Education goal, course of study, and exemption status default values

Using the Crosswalk Validation Page (GTVSDAX), you can define default values to be used for IDs that do not have respective data defined on the MIS Success and Support Services Historical Data Page (SVAMSHD) for the education goal (SS01) and exemption status (SS03, SS04, SS05, SS13, SS14, SS15) elements.

You can also use GTVSDAX entries for course of study to prevent values that are valid only for SP04 reporting from appearing in SS02 and SS12. The relevant GTVSDAX rows are shown in the following table. These GTVSDAX controls are provided to allow you to decide whether the IDs with missing data should be listed with space/filler or with another valid value of your choosing. During the CALBSTU install, the entries are loaded as shown with a null value in the Translation Code field.

Internal Code Internal Group External Code Translation Code Description
MIS_SS01 CALGEN ED_GOAL_DEFAULT null MIS SS01 default when unknown
MIS_SS02 CALGEN 99999 null MIS SS02 exclusion (SP04)
MIS_SS03 CALGEN ORN_EXM_DEFAULT null MIS SS03 default when unknown
MIS_SS04 CALGEN ASM_EXM_DEFAULT null MIS SS04 default when unknown
MIS_SS05 CALGEN EDP_EXM_DEFAULT null MIS SS05 default when unknown
MIS_SS12 CALGEN 99999 null MIS SS12 exclusion (SP04)
MIS_SS13 CALGEN ORN_EXM_DEFAULT null MIS SS13 default when unknown
MIS_SS14 CALGEN ASM_EXM_DEFAULT null MIS SS14 default when unknown
MIS_SS15 CALGEN EDP_EXM_DEFAULT null MIS SS15 default when unknown

For the GTVSDAX entries for education goal (SS01) and exemption status (SS03, SS04, SS05, SS13, SS14, SS15) as installed, this means that whenever an ID that is missing the data to complete any of these elements is reported on SS, that element will be reported with spaces (that is, “filler”) instead of an explicit value. For these elements, spaces/filler is not a valid value. By the current CCCCO DED definition, these elements do not have defined “unknown” values to handle situations where a student ID is included on the SS report but does not have the respective SVAMSHD data. Therefore, your SS report will fail the submission to the CCCCO until you update each problem ID with valid education goal and exemption status data. Alternatively, if you believe your policies and procedures can support and justify it, you can enter a default value for each element in the Translation Code field for each row. The default value must be one of the valid values for the respective element as defined on the CCCCO MIS DED. The value you enter will be the one you can support and defend to an auditor.

Take note of the following regarding how the education goal (SS01) and exemption status (SS03, SS04, SS05, SS13, SS14, SS15) GTVSDAX entries are used.

  • The value you enter in the Translation Code field for an element is the value that will be reported for IDs with no data for that element. Any value you enter in the Translation Code field must be a properly formatted valid value for the respective element per the CCCCO MIS DED.
  • If an empty (null) is specified in the Translation Code field, space/filler will be the value reported for the element. Space/filler is not a valid value in the DED and will fail the CCCCO upload. However, you can use this to identify student IDs with incomplete SVAMSHD data.
  • If the GTVSDAX entry for an element is removed or missing, the default will be space/filler.
  • Only the GTVSDAX record with the value 1 in the Sequence field (GTVSDAX_INTERNAL_CODE_SEQNO = 1) is used in the reporting of each of these elements. Any GTVSDAX record with a different value in the Sequence field is ignored.
The GTVSDAX entries for SS02 and SS12 are different than the ones above. To calculate SS02 and SS12 the logic will use data that mimics MIS SP report’s SP04 (Student-Program-Control-Number). However, SP04 allows values to be reported that are not valid in SS02 and SS12, such as ‘99999’. Therefore, if the SP04 data query finds such a value, a GTVSDAX entry allows the identification of it as not valid for MIS SS course of study reporting. This allow the search to continue for another possible valid value (SP01 Student-Program-Top-Code data). For the course of study (SS02, SS12), the GTVSDAX entries are used as follows:
  • The value you enter in the Translation Code field is the SP04 value that cannot be reported for SS02 or SS12 with no data for that element (’99999,’ ‘AAAAA’, ‘YYYYY’, etc.). Make one record for every SP04 value you use that cannot be reported in SS02, and make similar records for SS12.
  • If the GTVSDAX entries for SS02 and SS12 are removed or missing, all SP04 data found will be reported in SS02 or SS12. (This could cause MIS SS report data load problems.).
  • Multiple GTVSDAX entries are allowed for both SS02 and SS12.

If you delete any of these GTVSDAX entries and want to recreate them, manually enter the information specified above.

SS domain and record selection

The following records are included in the CALBSTU SS report output.

  • Every record on the SX report for the term and district/college specified when the SS report is run. For these students, SB_STU includes their SGASTDN and supporting data as normal. This applies to credit and noncredit students with data on SX.
  • Records that are not on SX but for which both of the following conditions are true.
    • The ID is for a student record (on SGASTDN with a past, current, or future effective term) or an applicant record (SAAADMS for a past, current, or future term). Each ID must be for a student or an applicant to complete the necessary CALBSTU SB_STU data. This applies to credit and noncredit IDs because a SB_STU record is required for all IDs.
    • There is at least one service (that is, at least one entry on any tab on SVAMSTD for the specified term and district/college). That entry could be a credit and noncredit service.
    • For these IDs, SB_STU includes the data from SGASTDN or SAAADMS, as noted in the Student Basic Data Report (SB_STU) for MIS section.
Entering SS specific data

The SS report is submitted using the Report Engine Run Page (GVAREPT) where you specify values for the district/college ID and term parameters. The following are the primary pages for the SS report services data.

  • MIS Success and Support Services Historical Data Page (SVAMSHD)
  • MIS Success and Support Services Term Data Page (SVAMSTD)

Both pages have the district/college ID in the key block, which is matched to the GVAREPT parameter. SVAMSHD is term effective, so term effective logic is used for the elements using its data. Both pages accommodate credit and noncredit data.

SVAMSTD is term specific, so the GVAREPT parameter must match the SVAMSTD key block term. This page is where you load the data that becomes part of the more complex elements on the SS report, specifically the ones that have the initial versus not initial calculations. For this reason, this page has the SS Report Preview tab, which will assist in verifying how the element values for term-specific services are calculated. How this works is explained in the details under each element in the How SS element values are calculated section.

Note: In CALBSTU 8.x, the SVAMSTD page has the SS Report Preview information defined on a separate tab with that same name. In CALBSTU 9.x, the SVAMSTD page has the SS Report Preview information defined in a section that displays at the bottom of each service data tab. Other than the location, the 8.x tab and 9.x section have the same information and function the same. Throughout this content, the wording will use the 8.x page references, but the explanations also apply to the 9.x pages.
How SS element values are calculated

The GI90, GI01, GI03, SB00, and SB02 elements are calculated and reported the same as for the other MIS reports. The calculations for the following elements are described in more detail in the succeeding sections.

Logic for determining three-year absence (initial elements)

If a service was initial, it means that it occurred for the first time ever for the ID or for the first time after a three-year or longer absence for the ID.

The phrase initial elements refers to the following pairs of elements. In each pairing, they have relationships where the one element can designate a service as initial while the other records the not initial service.

The logic considers credit vs. noncredit data separately, per the requirements of the regulation, by using MIS CB report's CB04 values to distinguish between the two. A student's attendance in noncredit classes and participation in noncredit services will not impact the three-year-absence status for credit services. Inversely, a student's attendance in credit classes and participation in credit services will not impact the three-year-absence status for noncredit services.

Orientation

Elements SS06 (credit) and SS16 (noncredit) only reports an initial orientation service. Credit vs. noncredit is determined by the service code setup.

Element SS11.1 reports non-initial orientation services, extra orientation services in the same term as initial services, or orientation services that cannot qualify as initial.

Assessment

Elements SS07 (credit) and SS17 (noncredit) only reports initial assessment services of one or more of the four distinct types. Credit vs. noncredit is determined by the service code setup.

Note: Elements SS07 and SS17 are positional and record data for up to four different types of assessment services. In this case, the initial designation applies to the whole element. For example, using the credit element, you cannot have an initial service for testing (position 2 of SS07) in one term and then report an initial service for any of the other three assessment types (the other three positions of SS07) in the next term or any term within the three-year absence range. To get credit for more than one assessment service type as initial, the services must all be in the same term and meet the conditions for initial within that term.

Elements SS11.2 (credit) and SS20.2 (noncredit) report non-initial assessment services, extra assessment services in the same term as initial services of the same type, or assessment services that cannot qualify as initial. It also reports career and interest services that do not report at all in element SS07 or SS17.

Education plan

For credit services, element SS09 reports combinations of services that result in an abbrethroughted or a comprehensive education plan.

About this task

Regarding element SS09's report value, the initial status matters only if the same term has both an initial abbrethroughted and initial comprehensive education plan, which results in the both (B) designation on the report. Both is used only if you have an initial abbrethroughted education plan in the same term as an initial comprehensive education plan. Per the CCCCO instructions (informal information that was communicated to Ellucian but not published explicitly in the CCCCO regulations), if only one of the two types is initial in this term while there is also a non-initial education plan service within this same term, you cannot use the both designation.

For noncredit services, element SS19 reports services that result in a noncredit education plan.

Elements SS11.3 (credit) and SS20.3 (noncredit) report non-initial education plan services, extra education plan services in the same term as initial services, or education plan services that cannot qualify as initial.

In a case where there is only one of the following, element SS11.3 indicates the initial designation by reporting a value of 0 (No).

  • An initial abbrethroughted education plan without any additional services
  • An initial comprehensive education plan without any additional services
  • Both an initial abbrethroughted and an initial comprehensive education plan (the both [B] designation)
    Note: Per CCCCO instructions, the education plan elements are unlike the orientation and assessment elements in that the "initial" designation depends on the precise combination of values in elements SS09 and SS11.3 or SS19 and SS20.3 instead of only the value in primary elements SS09 or SS19, respectively. There are also situations where it is impossible to detect an initial education plan service just by looking at the SS09 and SS11.3 results or at the SS19 and SS20.3 results. For credit, one such situation is when an initial abbrethroughted education plan (that is, SS09 is yes [A]) is in the same term as either an extra abbrethroughted plan or a follow-up/other service (that is, SS11.3 is yes [1]).

When evaluating a three-year absence, credit and noncredit data for services and for enrollment are completely separate, and each initial element is evaluated individually per the CCCCO instructions. In other words, the fact that credit orientation is not initial in this term has no bearing on the initial status for credit education plan and credit assessment, and vice versa. The same is true for noncredit. Additionally, the conditions to determine whether a service is initial or not depend on the student having at least a three-year absence specific to credit or noncredit. By design and the recommendation of the client focus group, the student type is not considered in this calculation.

The CALBSTU MIS SS report's design uses a conservative interpretation of a three-year absence. To qualify as absent for three years, the ID must meet the following requirements.

  • The ID was not enrolled, which means it was not reported on any SX report in the three years before the reporting term. The determination for credit vs. noncredit enrollment is determined by using the CB report's CB04 value for the SX record being considered.
  • The ID does not have recorded any similar initial-qualifying services within the prior three years of the service. This is specific to credit vs. noncredit for each service.

The first requirement was confirmed with the CCCCO. The second requirement regarding the absence of similar services is by design. Using other interpretations, it is not possible to clearly differentiate between absent and not absent from services in all combinations of service data for an ID. It would require a more complicated three-year absence evaluation where it would be possible to report a few IDs as having an initial service when the data would indicate that this is not true. Using the conservative definition of absent from enrollment and absent from similar services the results of the calculations are always the same and consistent, and therefore is the approach implemented in CALBSTU.

If a service, credit or noncredit, is defined as one that can potentially be initial, this means that you decided that it meets the regulatory qualifications, and, therefore, you loaded the service using a code that indicates this in its definition on the code's validation page (SVVEPST, SVVOSST, or SVVASST). To determine if a service with such a code can qualify as an initial service, there are two conditions to meet. The conditions are evaluated in the following order and methods.

Procedure

  1. Prior similar initial-qualifying services search: There are no prior similar initial-qualifying services within the three-year absence cutoff of the reporting term. This is accomplished within each initial element's calculation by the following sub-steps. These sub-steps use the credit orientation services and reporting term 201410 (Fall 2013) as an example, and that term has 201110 (Fall 2010) defined as its SVRTMIS enrollment cutoff term.
    1. The system searches for a prior similar initial-qualifying service starting in one term before the reporting term and descending backwards in time. For reporting term 201410, start with 201340 (Summer 2013) and look for the most recent credit orientation initial-qualifying service in or before 201340.
    2. If a similar initial-qualifying service is found not in any prior term (201340 or before), the reporting term's service qualifies as initial and is reported as such per its element definitions. No further searching is performed (neither sub-step 1.c nor step 2). In our example, this means no credit orientation services were found for this ID from 201340 backwards to the first or beginning of time term. SS06 is reported as yes (A). (The SS11.1 value will depend on whether extra services exist in this term.)
    3. If a similar credit initial-qualifying service is found in a prior term, the system calculates whether its term is within the three-year absence range by comparing the reporting term’s SVRTMIS enrollment cutoff term to the prior similar service's term.
      • If the prior service's term is greater than the cutoff term, the reporting term’s service does not qualify as initial and is reported as such per its element definitions. No further searching is performed (neither sub-step 1.c nor step 2). For our example in this case, let’s say that the prior credit orientation service’s term is 201310. because 201310 is greater than the 201110 cutoff for the reporting term, the reporting term cannot report the data as initial. SS06 is reported as no (N), and SS11.1 is reported as yes (1) for the current service.
      • However, if the prior service’s term is not greater than the cutoff term, the system cannot tell if the student has had a three-year absence by the service data alone. Now it must perform the credit enrollment search in step 2. For our example in this case, let's say the prior credit orientation service's term is 200910. because 200910 is not greater than the 201110 cutoff for the reporting term, the system cannot make a decision on the initial status as the data indicates it was possible to have a three-year absence gap. The enrollment search will provide the definitive answer.
  2. Enrollment search: As of the date on which you are running the SS report the ID was not reportable on any of the prior three year's SX reports with a SX record that had a CB record with a CB04 values that is credit. (The system does not use saved SX and CB report output results. It mimics the SX and CB report evaluations from the data that exists in Banner now.)

Results

As noted in step 1, this level of searching is only performed on the IDs for which the service data cannot by itself provide a definitive answer. This design helps system performance by not forcing a search through the registration data for every student on the SS report. However, there are additional measures taken in the actual code to improve performance. A key measure is that after any one service requires the enrollment search for an ID, an array is built for that ID of all terms before the reporting term that had SX enrollment or grade data. This prevents all three of the initial elements (orientation, assessment, and education plan) from performing a search on registration three times in the situation where all three of them have data that requires this search.

The major difference between the enrollment search and the prior similar initial-qualifying services search is that the prior similar services search stops as soon as it finds the most recent prior similar initial-qualifying service and evaluates it against the reporting term's cutoff. It is not necessary to continue looking for more services in other terms. The enrollment search, however, needs to approach the search differently because it is trying to determine whether there was a gap of three years in enrollment. While the system starts with one term before the reporting term with the intention of searching for the prior three years, every time it finds an enrollment, it must expand the search back at least one more term. (This might not be precisely one more term as it depends upon your institution's setups on SVRTMIS for the intersessions terms, as noted in the Online Help.)

The following series of examples illustrates this concept and the workings of this search.

The examples use reporting term 201410, and to simplify the examples and avoid confusion on interpreting intersession terms, only Fall and Spring terms (that is, two terms per academic year.) Therefore, the SVRTMIS setups are shown in the following table. SVRTMIS is used for all terms, and these examples would apply to credit or noncredit scenarios.
