SS01 Student Educational Goal

If a value exists in the Goal field of the Education Goals tab of SVAMSHD, that value is reported for this element.

The value reported is based on the record for which the value for the Goal Type field is Primary. (Only one record is allowed to be designated as Primary.) If no value exists, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS01 on GTVSDAX is reported. For details, see Education goal, course of study, and exemption status default values for more information about the GTVSDAX setting for this element.

If a primary goal is found, the code is converted into a MIS DED valid value for SS through the details you load on GVATRMP. The value in the Banner Value field is matched to your code, and the value in the Report Value field is reported. The report values you enter must be valid and properly formatted.

SS02 and SS12 Student Course of Study

SS02 reports credit data, and SS12 reports noncredit data.

The value reported for these elements is either the co-unique code for the ID's program or the TOP code for the ID’s major.

To distinguish between credit and noncredit data, the MIS SP report SP02 element GVATRMP data is used. GVATRMP is loaded with default values for SP02. According to the instructions for SP report, you will revise this as needed with your Banner values. (Refer to the Element SP02 STUDENT-PROGRAMAWARD section.) By the CCCCO MIS DED for SP02, the values of A, S, Y, Z, E, M, B, N, L, T, F, O are credit programs and the values of G, H, I, J, K, P, Q, R are noncredit programs. This will determine if a value can be reported in SS02 (credit) vs. SS12 (noncredit).

In order to report for a term a credit SS02 course of study and a noncredit SS12 course of study for a single ID, you must allow students to have more than active curriculum record at a time. This is by design and consistent with Banner Student functionality for curriculum. Inactive records are not used for MIS reporting.

For the reporting term, all active curriculum records are found. This list is sorted into a credit list and a noncredit list by the SP02 GVATRMP translation. From the credit list (if it has data), the current (if applicable), active, highest-priority record is reported in SS02. From the noncredit list (if it has data), the current (if applicable), active, highest-priority record is reported in SS12.

This data is selected by a baseline Student function based on the record used for reporting SB_STU data (the record used or searched for depends on which record is used to populate SB_STU data). The order of priority for completing the SB_STU element data is explained in the Student Basic Data Report (SB_STU) for MIS section. When the record is from SGASTDN, the data is found on the respective curriculum (LMOD = LEARNER) record. When the record is from SAAADMS, the data is found on the respective curriculum (LMOD = ADMISSIONS) record.

If no co-unique or TOP code is found from these sources and all three of the exemption elements (SS03, SS04, and SS05 for credit or SS13, SS14, and SS15 for noncredit) have any combination of the exempt values (DY, OY, DO, and OD, which represent 'not referred to services'), the 'exempt' value (YYYYYY) is reported for the respective element (credit SS02 or noncredit SS12).

For details, see Education goal, course of study, and exemption status default values section for information on the GTVSDAX entries for SS02 and SS12.

SS03 and SS13 Student Initial Orientation Exempt Status

SS03 reports credit data, and SS13 reports noncredit data.

If a value exists in the respective Initial Orientation Status field of the Exempt Status tab of SVAMSHD, that value is reported for this element. If no value exists for credit reporting, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS03 on GTVSDAX is reported. If no value exists for noncredit reporting, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS13 on GTVSDAX is reported. Refer to Education goal, course of study, and exemption status default values for more information about the GTVSDAX setting for this element.

SS04 and SS14 Student Initial Assessment Exempt Status

SS04 reports credit data, and SS14 reports noncredit data.

If a value exists in the respective Initial Assessment Status field of the Exempt Status tab of SVAMSHD, that value is reported for this element. If no value exists for credit reporting, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS04 on GTVSDAX is reported. If no value exists for noncredit reporting, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS14 on GTVSDAX is reported. Refer to Education goal, course of study, and exemption status default values for more information about the GTVSDAX setting for this element.

SS05 and SS15 Student Education Plan Exempt Status

SS05 reports credit data, and SS15 reports noncredit data.

If a value exists in the respective Education Plan Status field of the Exempt Status tab of SVAMSHD, that value is reported for this element. If no value exists for credit reporting, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS05 on GTVSDAX is reported. If no value exists for noncredit reporting, the value defined for internal code MIS_SS15 on GTVSDAX is reported. Refer to Education goal, course of study, and exemption status default values for more information about the GTVSDAX setting for this element.

SS06/SS16 Initial Orientation and SS11.1/SS20.1 Orientation

SS06 and SS11.1 report credit data, and SS16 and SS20.1 report noncredit data.

SS11.1 is the notation used to designate the SS11 element position 1, and SS20.1 is the notation used to designate the SS20 element position 1. This notation is used in the SVAMSTD field label. The phrases reporting term and this term refer to the term specified in the key block of SVAMSTD or the term specified when the SS report was run. The references to View Calculation Details refer to the buttons on SVAMSTD. The phrase data window refers to the data window that is displayed when you click View Calculation Details for the specified element.

SS06 and SS11.1 are a pair of elements used to report credit orientation services data for the reporting term. SS16 and SS20.1 are a pair of elements used to report noncredit orientation services data for the reporting term. The data for these elements is loaded on SVAMSTD. For the credit and noncredit sets, they have a complicated calculation process with a relationship to each other. To help research or confirm a result on the SS report output for these elements, you can view the values that will be reported for them by clicking Calculate in SS Report Preview tab.

If you click View Calculation Details for one of these fields, the system displays a data window that explains how the result was calculated and the data that was found to support it. The next section explains how the details in the data window are calculated.

Calculation logic for initial elements SS06/SS11.1 and SS16/SS20.1

This section describes the calculation logic for initial credit elements SS06 and SS11.1 and initial noncredit elements SS16 and SS20.1.

About this task

To simplify the explanations, the references to reported values include only the codes. Additionally, the only difference between credit and noncredit is the SVVOSST noncredit service indicator. That setting determines if the data will be reported as credit or noncredit orientation services.

Because credit logic and noncredit logic are identical, only a credit example is shown. The following table provides the text meanings of the codes, using the credit example.

Code Description
SS06 (or SS16)
A “Yes,” the student did participate in initial-qualifying orientation services.
N “No,” the student did not participate in initial-qualifying orientation services.
SS11.1 (or SS20.1)
0 No, no reportable services were provided.
1 Yes, reportable services were provided.

The calculations for the SS06 and SS11.1 elements are as follows. (SS16 and SS20.1 are similar.)

The SS06 and SS11.1 elements are initialized to their respective no values: N and 0.

Procedure

  1. If no credit record exists on the Orientation tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term, the SS06 element is reported with the value N and the SS11.1 element is reported with the value 0. The data window for each element displays a message indicating there are no reportable services in this term. No further searching is performed.
  2. If the only credit services listed for this term are coded as not being initial-qualifying (that is, the Qualifying Initial Orientation check box on SVVOSST is unchecked), the SS06 element is reported with the value N, and the data window for the SS06 element displays a message indicating there are no reportable services. The SS11.1 element is reported with the value 1 and the data window for the SS11.1 element displays a message noting that only non-initial-qualifying services exist. No further searching is performed.
  3. If there are credit services listed for this term coded as being initial-qualifying (that is, the Qualifying Initial Orientation check box is checked), the calculation searches for prior initial-qualifying services including the evaluation for three-year absence. This search is detailed in section Logic for determining three-year absence (initial elements).
    1. If the search in step 3 returns the results that the reporting term’s credit service can be reported as the initial service, the SS06 is reported with the value A, and the data window for the SS06 element displays a message noting that such a service exists and provides the service’s details.

      To determine the SS11.1 value, the system now checks whether there are any extra credit services of any type that can be reported as an extra or follow-up service in this term.

      • If the record count for credit orientation services in this term is greater than 1 (the Qualifying Initial Orientation check box setting does not matter at this point), the SS11.1 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term has extra services, and the data window for the SS11.1 element displays a message indicating a service exists that was not reported in SS06 and provides the service’s details. No further searching is performed.
        Note: The system does not use the same credit record to report A for the SS06 element and to report 1 for the SS11.1 element.
      • If the record count for credit orientation services is not greater than 1, the SS11.1 element is reported as 0, and the data window for the SS11.1 element displays a message indicating that no services exists that were not reported in the SS06 element. No further searching is performed.
    2. If the search in step 3 returns the results that this term’s credit service cannot be reported as the initial service, the following results are reported.
      • The SS06 element is reported as N, and the data window for the SS06 element displays a message indicating that although this term does have initial-qualifying credit services, they cannot be reported as the initial service because a prior service exists without a three-year absence. It includes the prior term’s service details to provide proof of why this term’s services cannot be initial.
      • The SS11.1 element is reported as 1 because this term’s credit service is considered an extra or follow-up service in this situation, and the data window for the SS11.1 element displays a message indicating a service exists that was not reported in the SS06 element and provides the services details. No further searching is performed.
    3. If your SVRTMIS data is not complete for all terms, the search in step 3 cannot finish its evaluation when the credit enrollment search is required. In this case, the SS06 and SS11.1 elements are both reported as spaces/filler, and the data window for the each of these elements displays a message indicating that the calculation could not be completed because a term is missing its enrollment cutoff. (The missing term is specified in the message.)

      The CALBSTU installation includes the svrtmis_report_080901.sql script that you can use to verify that all of your terms are defined on SVRTMIS. Use this script as needed to save time by finding all the terms missing from the SVRTMIS setups.

      Note: Because not all IDs listed on the SS report require the credit enrollment search, there will be cases where some IDs have spaces/filler reported with this error while other IDs list valid results. Additionally, because not all IDs require a search of the same range of terms in the enrollment search, you can see differences is this respect, too. One ID might require a search of only five years' worth of terms and not encounter an error, while another requires a search of 10 years' worth of terms and does encounter an error.
SS07/SS17 Initial Assessment and SS11.2/SS20.2 Assessment/Career/Interest

SS07 and SS11.2 report credit data, and SS17 and SS20.2 report noncredit data.

SS11.2 is the notation used to designate the SS11 element position 2, and SS20.2 is the notation used to designate the SS20 element position 2. This notation is used in the SVAMSTD field label. The phrases reporting term and this term refer to the term specified in the key block of SVAMSTD or the term specified when the SS report was run. The references to View Calculation Details refer to the buttons on SVAMSTD. The phrase data window refers to the data window that is displayed when you click View Calculation Details for the specified element.

SS07 and SS11.2 are a pair of elements used to report credit assessment services data for the reporting term. SS17 and SS20.2 are a pair of elements used to report noncredit assessment services data for the reporting term. The SS11.2 and SS20.2 elements additionally report career and interest information. The data for these elements is loaded on SVAMSTD. For the credit and noncredit sets, they have a complicated calculation process with a relationship to each other. To help research or confirm a result on the SS report output for these elements, you can view the values that will be reported for them by clicking Calculate in the SS Report Preview tab.

If you click View Calculation Details for one of these fields, the system displays a data window that explains how the result was calculated and the data that was found to support it. The next section explains how the details in the data window are calculated.

Calculation logic for initial elements SS07/SS11.2 and SS17/SS20.2

This section describes the calculation logic for initial elements credit SS07 and SS11.2 and initial noncredit elements SS17 and SS20.2.

About this task

To simplify the explanations, the references to reported values include only the codes. Additionally, the only difference between credit and noncredit is the SVVASST noncredit service indicator. That setting determines if the data will be reported as credit or noncredit assessment services.

Because credit logic and noncredit logic are identical, only a credit example is shown. The following table provides the text meanings of the codes, using the credit example.

SS07 (or SS17) is a positional element with four separate yes/no values. Each position reports the applicable one-character value for that type of service. For example, the value 0010 means that no reportable and initial-qualifying services were provided for the types of services in positions 1, 2, and 4, while a reportable and initial-qualifying services was provided for the type of service in position 3.

The positions are as follows.

  • Position 1: Student received placement services based on alternative measures in lieu of an assessment test.
  • Position 2: Student received placement services based on assessment testing and alternate multiple measures.
  • Position 3: Student received placement services based on placement results from other college or university.
  • Position 4: Student received placement services based on Early Assessment Program (EAP) test results.
Code Description
0 “No,” no reportable and initial-qualifying services were provided.
1 “Yes,” reportable and initial-qualifying services were provided.
SS11.2 (or SS20.2)  
0 “No,” no reportable services were provided.
1 “Yes,” reportable services were provided.

The calculations for the SS07 and SS11.2 elements are as follows. (SS17 and SS20.2 are similar.)

The SS07 and SS11.2 elements are initialized to their respective “no” values: 0000 (“no” in all four positions) and 0.

Note: After the SS11.2 element is set to 1 for any reason, it cannot be reset to 0. The value can be changed from 0 to 1 later in the calculations, but it cannot be changed from 1 to 0.

Procedure

  1. The SS11.2 element reports the credit career or interest service data that is unrelated to the SS07 element. If any credit records exist on the Career/Interest tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term, the SS11.2 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for the SS11.2 element displays a message noting that career or services exists.

    The calculation must continue with step 2 to evaluate the credit assessment services for the SS07 and SS11.2 elements. If any credit assessment data is found that could be reported in the SS11.2 element, it is noted in the data window in addition to what was found for career or interest. The SS11.2 element can only report 1. However, by noting that there are both career or interest services in addition to other assessment services for SS11.2, it is providing the complete picture of all reasons why SS11.2 can be reported as 1.

  2. If no credit record exists on the Assessment tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term, the SS07 element is reported with the value 0000.

    The SS11.2 element is reported with the value 0 if there were also no reportable credit career or interest to report from step 1.

    The data window for each of these elements displays a message indicating there are no reportable credit assessment services in this term. (Even if the SS11.2 element is already 1 because of career or interest services, the additional notation is made regarding the lack of assessment services.)

    No further searching is performed.

  3. If the only credit services listed for this term are coded as non-initial-qualifying (that is, the value in the Assessment Service field for the code on SVVASST is Assessment for Other Disciplines), the SS07 element is reported with the value 0000, and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message indicating there are no reportable services. The SS11.2 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for the SS11.2 element displays a message noting that only non-initial-qualifying services exist. (This is added to the SS11.2 career or interest details.) No further searching is performed.
  4. If there are credit services listed that are coded as being initial-qualifying (that is, the value in the Assessment Service field for the code on SVVASST is Alternative Measure, Early Assessment Program (EAP), Other Institution Placement, or Testing) for this term, the calculation searches for prior initial-qualifying services including the evaluation for three-year absence. This search is explained in Logic for determining three-year absence (initial elements).
    1. If the search in step 4 returns the results that the reporting term’s credit service can be reported as the initial service, the SS07 element is reported with the value 1, but the precise configuration of the “yes” value must be calculated. At the end of this calculation, one or more of the four positions of SS07 is reported with the value 1, and the data window displays the supporting details for each position (that is, whether a service exists or not for each type of placement service).
      • For the SS07.1 element (that is, SS07 position 1):
      • If the reporting term has at least one credit service whose SVVASST assessment service type is Alternative Measure, the SS07.1 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message noting that such a service exists and provides the service’s details.
      • If no credit Alternative Measure records exist in this term, the SS07.1 element is reported with the value 0, and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message noting that no such a service exists in the term.
      • For the SS07.2 element:
      • If the reporting term has at least one credit service whose SVVASST assessment service type is Testing, the SS07.2 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for SS07 element displays a message noting that such a service exists and provides the service’s details.
      • If no credit Testing records exist in this term, the SS07.2 element is reported with the value 0, and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message noting that no such a service exists in the term.
      • For the SS07.3 element:
      • If the reporting term has at least one credit service whose SVVASST assessment service type is Other Institution Placement, the SS07.3 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for SS07 element displays a message noting that such a service exists and provides the service’s details.
      • If no credit Other Institution Placement records exist in this term, the SS07.3 element is reported with the value 0, and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message noting that no such a service exists in the term.
      • For the SS07.4 element:
      • If the reporting term has at least one credit service whose SVVASST assessment service type is Early Assessment Program (EAP), the SS07.4 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for SS07 element displays a message noting that such a service exists and provides the service’s details.
      • If no credit Early Assessment Program (EAP) records exist in this term, the SS07.4 element is reported with the value 0, and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message noting that no such a service exists in the term.
      • To determine the SS11.2 value, the system now checks whether there are any extra credit services of any type that can be reported as an extra or follow-up service in this term. This occurs in one of the following ways.
      • If either there is non-initial-qualifying credit service (that is, the value in the Assessment Service field for the code on SVVASST is Assessment for Other Disciplines) or any extra credit services of the other four types (an extra service that was not already reported for the SS07 element), the SS11.2 element is reported as 1 because the reporting term has extra services. The data window for the SS11.2 element displays a message indicating a service exists that was not reported for the SS07 element and provides the service’s details. (This is added to the SS11.2 career or interest details.)

        No further searching is performed.

        Note: The system does not use the same credit record to report 1 in any position for the SS07 element and to report 1 for the SS11.2 element.
      • If there is no non-initial-qualifying credit service (that is, the value in the Assessment Service field for the code on SVVASST is Assessment for Other Disciplines) and there are no extra credit services of the other four types (an extra service that was not already reported for the SS07 element), the SS11.2 element is reported with a value of 0 (as long as there were also no reportable career or interest to report from step 1), and the data window for the SS11.2 element displays a message indicating that no services exists that were not reported for the SS07 element. (This is added to the SS11.2 career or interest details.)

        No further searching is performed.

    2. If the search in step 4 returns the results that this term’s credit service cannot be reported as the initial service, the following results are reported.
      • The SS07 element is reported with a value of 0000 (No), and the data window for the SS07 element displays a message indicating that while this term does have initial-qualifying credit services, they cannot be reported as the initial service because a prior service exists without a three-year absence. The message includes the prior term’s service details to provide proof of why this term’s services cannot be initial.
      • The SS11.2 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term’s credit service is considered an extra or follow-up service in this situation, and the data window for the SS11.2 element displays a message indicating a service exists that was not reported in SS07 and provides the service’s details. (This is added to the SS11.2 career or interest details.) No further searching is performed.
    3. If your SVRTMIS data is not complete for all terms, the search in step 4 cannot finish its evaluation when the credit enrollment search is required. In this case, the SS07 and SS11.2 elements are both reported as spaces/filler, and the data window for each element displays a message indicating that the calculation could not be completed because a term is missing its enrollment cutoff. (The missing term is specified in the message.)

      The CALBSTU installation includes the svrtmis_report_080901.sql script that you can use to verify that all of your terms are defined on SVRTMIS. Use this script as needed to save time by finding all the terms missing from the SVRTMIS setups.

      Note: Because not all IDs listed on the SS report require the credit enrollment search, there will be cases where some IDs have spaces/filler reported with this error while other IDs list valid results. Additionally, because not all IDs require a search of the same range of terms in the enrollment search, you can see differences is this respect, too. One ID might require a search of only five years' worth of terms and not encounter an error, while another requires a search of 10 years' worth of terms and does encounter an error.
SS08 and SS18 Counseling/Advisement

SS08 reports credit data, and SS18 reports noncredit data.

The services are coded and reported as credit vs. noncredit by the SVVCOST noncredit service indicator. That setting determines if the data will be reported as credit or noncredit counseling/advisement services.

If at least one credit service record exists on the Counsel/Advise tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term (the term in the key block of SVAMSTD or the term specified when the SS report was run), the SS08 credit element is reported as the value that represents yes. SS18 for noncredit works similarly.

Values for SS08 and SS18 are as follows:
  • A: Student received counseling/advisement services during the reporting term
  • N: Student did not participate in counseling or advisement services during the reporting term

The data for this element is loaded on SVAMSTD. To help research or confirm a result on the SS report output for it, you can view the values that will be reported for these elements by clicking Calculate in the SS Report Preview tab.

If you click View Calculation Details for this field, the system displays a data window that explains how the result was calculated and the data that was found to support it.

SS09/SS19 Education Plan and SS11.3/SS20.3 Education Plan

SS09 and SS11.3 report credit data, and SS19 and SS20.3 report noncredit data.

SS11.3 is the notation used to designate the SS11 element position 3, and SS20.3 is the notation used to designate the SS20 element position 3. This notation is used in the SVAMSTD field label. The phrases reporting term and this term refer to the term specified in the key block of SVAMSTD or the term specified when the SS report was run. The references to View Calculation Details refer to the buttons on SVAMSTD. The phrase “data window” refers to the data window that is displayed when you click View Calculation Details for the specified element.

SS09 and SS11.3 are a pair of elements used to report credit education plan data for the reporting term. SS19 and SS20.3 are a pair of elements used to report noncredit education plan data for the reporting term. The data for these elements is loaded on SVAMSTD. For the credit and noncredit sets, they have a complicated calculation process with a relationship to each other. To help research or confirm a result on the SS report output for these elements, you can view the values that will be reported for these elements by clicking Calculate in the SS Report Preview tab of SVAMSTD.

If you click View Calculation Details for one of these fields, the system displays a data window that explains how the result was calculated and the data that was found to support it. The next section explains how the details in the data window are calculated.

Calculation logic for initial credit elements SS09 and SS11.3

This section describes the calculation logic for initial credit elements SS09 and SS11.3. Because of the significant differences in the noncredit elements, they are described separately.

About this task

To simplify the explanations, the references to reported values include only the codes. The following table provides the text meanings of the codes, which are defined on SVVEPST with a credit type of service.

Code Description
SS09
A The student developed an abbrethroughted education plan (initial or not).
B The student developed an abbrethroughted and a comprehensive education plan. This is only used when both the abbrethroughted and the comprehensive education plan are initial of each type. It is not used if only one of them is the initial of its type while the other is not the initial of its type. (This is per CCCCO instructions.)
C The student developed a comprehensive education plan (initial or not).
N The student did not complete an education plan during the term.
SS11.3  
0 No, either no reportable extra or follow-up services were provided or the A, C, or B value reported for the SS09 element is an initial service.
1 Yes, reportable extra or follow-up services were provided or the A or C value reported for the SS09 element is not an initial service.

In the remainder of this section, all references to services and enrollment are credit only.

The SS09 and SS11.3 valid value relationship is not consistent with the CCCCO design for the SS06/SS11.1 and SS07/SS11.2 elements. SS09 is not purely an initial element, while the SS06 and SS07 elements are. With SS06 and SS07, the same data reported as Yes in those elements cannot be used to cause a Yes result in the respective SS11 positions. This is not the case with the SS09 and SS11.3 elements. In some circumstances, SS09 has a value of A or C (which both represent Yes) and SS11.3 has a value of 1 (which also represents Yes), and those respective Yes values are related to the same record in this term. This is per the instructions and regulations of the CCCCO.

Because of the complexities of the SS09 and SS11.3 calculations and the element relationships, the explanations in data window for each of these elements are very detailed and can be quite long. In SS11.3 in particular, there might be several reasons provided for why the yes result is valid.

The calculations for the SS09 and SS11.3 elements are as follows.

SS09 and SS11.3 are initialized to their respective no values: N and 0.

Note: After the SS11.3 element is set to 1 for any reason, it cannot be reset to 0. The value can be changed from 0 to 1later in the calculations, but it cannot be changed from 1 to 0.

Procedure

  1. If no record exists on the Education Plan tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term, the SS09 element is reported with the value N and the SS11.3 element is reported with the value 0, and the data window for each of the elements displays a message indicating there are no reportable services in this term. No further searching is performed.
  2. If the only services listed for this term are coded as not being other or follow-up (that is, the value in the Education Plan Service field on SVVEPST is Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan), the SS09 element is reported with the value N, and the data window for the SS09 element displays a message indicating there are no abbrethroughted or comprehensive services. The SS11.3 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window displays a message noting the other or follow-up service’s details. No further searching is performed.
  3. If the services listed for this term include a mixture that includes at least one service whose SVVASST education plan service type is Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan and any number of services whose education plan service type is Credit Abbrethroughted Plan or Credit Comprehensive Plan, the SS11.3 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for SS11.3 element displays a message noting the other or follow-up service’s details.

    The calculation continues to determine the remaining details. The calculation for abbrethroughted education plans (SS09=A) is first, and the calculation for comprehensive education plans (SS09=C) is second because it has a higher priority in SS09 reporting. A value of A for element SS09 can be replaced by C when both service types exist. However, the results of the A calculation are critical and necessary to determine whether the value B for the SS09 element is appropriate.

  4. A Search: If there are services whose SVVEPST education plan service type is Credit Abbrethroughted Plan for this term, the calculation searches for prior initial-qualifying Credit Abbrethroughted Plan services including the evaluation for a credit three-year absence. This search is explained in Logic for determining three-year absence (initial elements). In this case, the search looks exclusively for prior Credit Abbrethroughted Plan services. (It does not looking for prior Credit Comprehensive Plan services.)
    1. If the search in step 4 returns the results that the reporting term’s Credit Abbrethroughted Plan service can be reported as the initial service, the SS09 element is reported with a value of A, and the SS11.3 value is reported with a value of 0, although if SS11.3 was already 1 because the calculation in step 3 (Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan), it is not changed. The data window for SS09 element displays a message noting that a Credit Abbrethroughted Plan service that it is the initial service of this type exists and provides the service's details. The system also keeps track that this was an initial A service because this information is needed to calculate the B value later.

      To determine the value for the SS11.3 element, the system now checks whether there are any extra Credit Abbrethroughted Plan services that can be reported as an extra or follow-up service in this term.

      • If the record count for Credit Abbrethroughted Plan services in this term is greater than 1, the SS11.3 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term has extra services. The data window for SS11.3 element displays a message indicating a service exists that was not reported for the SS09 element and provides the service’s details. (This is in addition to anything noted for a Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan if one was found in step 3.) The A Search ends and the system continues with the C Search in step 5.
      • If the record count for Credit Abbrethroughted Plan is not greater than 1, the SS11.3 element is reported with a value of 0, although if SS11.3 was already 1 because the calculation in step 3, it is not changed. The data window for SS11.3 element displays a message indicating that no extra Credit Abbrethroughted Plan services exists that were not reported for the SS09 element. The A Search ends and the system continues with the C Search in step 5.
    2. If the search in step 4 returns the results that this term’s Credit Abbrethroughted Plan service cannot be reported as the initial service, the following results are reported.
      • The SS09 element is reported with a value of A, and the data window for SS09 element displays a message indicating that while this term does have Credit Abbrethroughted Plan services, it cannot be reported as the initial service because a prior service exists without a three-year absence. The message also provides the prior term’s service details to explain why this term’s services cannot be “initial.”
      • The SS11.3 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term’s service is considered an extra or follow-up service in this situation. The data window for SS11.3 element displays a message indicating that an Credit Abbrethroughted Plan service exists that is not an initial service of this type, and provides the service’s details. (This is in addition to anything noted for an Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan if one was found in 3.)

        The A Search ends and the system continues with the C Search in step 5.

  5. C Search: If there are services whose SVVEPST education plan service type is Credit Comprehensive Plan for this term, the calculation searches for prior initial-qualifying Credit Comprehensive Plan services including the evaluation for a three-year absence. This search is explained in Logic for determining three-year absence (initial elements). In this case, the search looks exclusively for prior Credit Comprehensive Plan services.
    1. If the search in step 5 returns the results that the reporting term’s Credit Comprehensive Plan service can be reported as the initial service, the SS09 element is reported with a value of C (which might mean that A is being replaced by C as required by CCCCO instructions), and the SS11.3 element is reported with a value of 0, although if SS11.3 was already 1 because of the calculations in steps 3 (Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan) and 4 (Credit Abbrethroughted Plan), it is not changed. The data window for SS09 element displays a message noting that a Credit Comprehensive Plan service exists and that it is the initial service of this type, and provides the service’s details. (This is in addition to anything noted for a Credit Abbrethroughted Plan in step 4.) The system also keeps track that this was an initial C service because this information is needed to calculate the B value later.

      To determine the value for the SS11.3 element, the system now checks whether there are any extra Credit Comprehensive Plan services that can be reported as an extra or follow-up service in this term.

      • If the record count for Credit Comprehensive Plan services in this term is greater than 1, the SS11.3 element is reported with the value 1 because this term has extra services. The data window for SS11.3 element displays a message indicating that a service exists that was not reported for the SS09 element, and provides the service’s details. (This is in addition to anything noted for an Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan if one was found in step 3 and in addition to anything noted for an Credit Abbrethroughted Plan in step 4.) The C Search ends and the system continues with the B Search in step 6.
      • If the record count for Credit Comprehensive Plan services is not greater than 1, the SS11.3 element is reported with a value of 0, although if SS11.3 was already 1 because the calculations in steps 3 (Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan) and 4 (Credit Abbrethroughted Plan), it is not changed. The data window for SS11.3 element displays a message indicating that no extra Credit Comprehensive Plan services exists that were not reported for the SS09 element. The C Search ends and the system continues with the B Search in step 6.
    2. If the search in step 5 returns the results that this term’s Credit Comprehensive Plan service cannot be reported as the initial service, the following results are reported.
      • The SS09 element is reported with a value of C (which might mean that A is being replaced by C as required by CCCCO instructions). The data window for SS09 element displays a message indicating that although this term has Credit Comprehensive Plan services, it cannot be reported as the initial service because a prior service exists without a three-year absence. It includes the prior term’s service details to explain why this term’s services cannot be “initial.”
      • The SS11.3 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term’s service is considered an extra or follow-up service in this situation. The data window for SS11.3 element displays a message indicating that a Credit Comprehensive Plan service exists that is not an initial service of this type, and provides the service’s details. (This is in addition to anything noted for an Credit Other or Follow-Up Plan if one was found in step 3 and in addition to anything noted for an Credit Abbrethroughted Plan in step 4.)

        The C Search ends and the system continues with the B Search in step 6.

  6. B Search: As a final step, the system determines whether the SS09 element can be B (Both). If the result of the A Search in step 4 (Credit Abbrethroughted Plan) noted that this was an initial A and the result of the C Search step 5 (Credit Comprehensive Plan) noted that this was an initial C, the value for the SS09 element is changed to B, and the data window for SS09 displays a final notation that both service types were “initial.”
  7. If your SVRTMIS data is not complete for all terms, the A search in step 4 (Credit Abbrethroughted Plan) and the C search in step 5 (Credit Comprehensive Plan) cannot finish their evaluations when the enrollment search is required. In this case, the SS09 and SS11.3 elements are both reported as spaces/filler. The data window for each element displays a message indicating that the calculation could not be completed because a term is missing its enrollment cutoff. (The missing term is specified in the message.)

    The CALBSTU installation includes the svrtmis_report_080901.sql script that you can use to verify that all of your terms are defined on SVRTMIS. Use this script as needed to save time by finding all the terms missing from the SVRTMIS setups.

    Note: Because not all IDs listed on the SS report require the enrollment search, there will be cases where some IDs have spaces/filler reported with this error while other IDs list valid results. Additionally, because not all IDs require a search of the same range of terms in the enrollment search, you can see differences is this respect, too. One ID might require a search of only five years' worth of terms and not encounter an error, while another requires a search of 10 years' worth of terms and does encounter an error.
Calculation logic for initial noncredit elements SS19 and SS20.3

This section describes the calculation logic for initial noncredit elements SS19 and SS20.3. Because of the significant differences in the credit elements, they are described separately.

About this task

To simplify the explanations, the references to reported values include only the codes. The following table provides the text meanings of the codes, which are defined on SVVEPST with a noncredit type of service.

Code Description
SS19
A The student developed a noncredit education plan (initial or not).
N The student did not complete a noncredit education plan during the term.
SS20.3
0 No, either no reportable extra or follow-up services were provided or the A value reported for the SS19 element is an initial service.
1 Yes, reportable extra or follow-up services were provided or the A value reported for the SS19 element is not an initial service.

In the remainder of this section, all references to services and enrollment are noncredit only.

The SS19 and SS20.3 valid value relationship is not consistent with the CCCCO design for the SS16/SS20.1 and SS17/SS20.2 elements. SS19 is not purely an initial element, while the SS16 and SS17 elements are. With SS16 and SS17, the same data reported as Yes in those elements cannot be used to cause a Yes result in the respective SS20 positions. This is not the case with the SS19 and SS20.3 elements. In some circumstances, SS19 has a value of A (which represents Yes) and SS20.3 has a value of 1 (which also represents Yes), and those respective Yes values are related to the same record in this term. This is per the instructions and regulations of the CCCCO.

Because of the complexities of the SS19 and SS20.3 calculations and the element relationships, the explanations in data window for each of these elements are very detailed and can be quite long. In SS20.3 in particular, there might be several reasons provided for why the Yes result is valid.

The calculations for the SS19 and SS20.3 elements are as follows. SS19 and SS20.3 are initialized to their respective no values: N and 0.

Note: After the SS20.3 element is set to 1 for any reason, it cannot be reset to 0. The value can be changed from 0 to 1 later in the calculations, but it cannot be changed from 1 to 0.

Procedure

  1. If no record exists on the Education Plan tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term, the SS19 element is reported with the value N and the SS20.3 element is reported with the value 0, and the data window for each of the elements displays a message indicating there are no reportable services in this term. No further searching is performed.
  2. If the only services listed for this term are coded as not being other or follow-up (that is, the value in the Education Plan Service field on SVVEPST is Noncredit Other or Follow-Up Plan), the SS19 element is reported with the value N, and the data window for the SS19 element displays a message indicating there are no qualifying noncredit education plan services. The SS20.3 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window displays a message noting the other or follow-up service's details. No further searching is performed.
  3. If the services listed for this term include a mixture that includes at least one service whose SVVASST education plan service type is Noncredit Other or Follow-Up Plan and any number of services whose education plan service type is Noncredit Plan, the SS20.3 element is reported with the value 1, and the data window for SS20.3 element displays a message noting the other or follow-up service's details.

    The calculation continues to determine the remaining details.

  4. If there are services whose SVVEPST education plan service type is Noncredit Plan for this term, the calculation searches for prior initial-qualifying Noncredit Plan services including the evaluation for a noncredit three-year absence. This search is explained in Logic for determining three-year absence (initial elements). In this case, the search looks exclusively for prior Noncredit Plan services.
    1. If the search in step 4 returns the results that the reporting term's Noncredit Plan service can be reported as the initial service, the SS19 element is reported with a value of A, and the SS20.3 value is reported with a value of 0, although if SS20.3 was already 1 because the calculation in step 3 (Noncredit Other or Follow-Up Plan), it is not changed. The data window for SS19 element displays a message noting that an Noncredit Plan service that it is the initial service of this type exists and provides the service’s details.

      To determine the value for the SS20.3 element, the system now checks whether there are any extra Noncredit Plan services that can be reported as an extra or follow-up service in this term.

      • If the record count for Noncredit Plan services in this term is greater than 1, the SS20.3 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term has extra services. The data window for SS20.3 element displays a message indicating a service exists that was not reported for the SS19 element and provides the service’s details. (This is in addition to anything noted for a Noncredit Other or Follow-Up Plan if one was found in step 3.)
      • If the record count for Noncredit Plan is not greater than 1, the SS20.3 element is reported with a value of 0, although if SS20.3 was already 1 because the calculation in step 3, it is not changed. The data window for SS20.3 element displays a message indicating that no extra Noncredit Plan services exists that were not reported for the SS19 element.
    2. If the search in 4 returns the results that this term’s Noncredit Plan service cannot be reported as the initial service, the following results are reported.
      • The SS19 element is reported with a value of A, and the data window for SS19 element displays a message indicating that while this term does have Noncredit Plan services, it cannot be reported as the initial service because a prior service exists without a three-year absence.
      • The message also provides the prior term’s service details to explain why this term's services cannot be initial.
      • The SS20.3 element is reported with a value of 1 because this term’s service is considered an extra or follow-up service in this situation. The data window for SS20.3 element displays a message indicating that a Noncredit Plan service exists that is not an initial service of this type, and provides the service's details. (This is in addition to anything noted for a Noncredit Other or Follow-Up Plan if one was found in 3.)
  5. If your SVRTMIS data is not complete for all terms, 4 cannot finish the evaluation when the noncredit enrollment search is required. In this case, the SS19 and SS20.3 elements are both reported as spaces/filler. The data window for each element displays a message indicating that the calculation could not be completed because a term is missing its enrollment cutoff. (The missing term is specified in the message.)

    The CALBSTU installation includes the svrtmis_report_080901.sql script that you can use to verify that all of your terms are defined on SVRTMIS. Use this script as needed to save time by finding all the terms missing from the SVRTMIS setups.

    Note: Because not all IDs listed on the SS report require the noncredit enrollment search, there will be cases where some IDs have spaces/filler reported with this error while other IDs list valid results. Additionally, because not all IDs require a search of the same range of terms in the enrollment search, you can see differences is this respect, too. One ID might require a search of only five years' worth of terms and not encounter an error, while another requires a search of 10 years' worth of terms and does encounter an error.
SS10 Academic Progress and SS11.4 Academic/Progress Probation

SS10 and SS11.4 report credit data. There are no noncredit equivalents.

SS11.4 is the notation used to designate the SS11 element position 4. This notation is used in the SVAMSTD page field label. The phrases reporting term and this term refer to the term specified in the key block of SVAMSTD or the term specified when the SS report was run. The references to View Calculation Details refer to the buttons on SVAMSTD. The phrase data window refers to the data window that is displayed when you click View Calculation Details for the specified element.

SS10 and SS11.4 are a pair of elements used to report academic progress and probation services data for the reporting term. They report similar data, but they do not duplicate the same data record. Each element reports data for a record unique to it. To help research or confirm a result on the SS report output for these elements, you can view the values that will be reported for these elements by clicking Calculate in the SS Report Preview tab of SVAMSTD.

If you click View Calculation Details for one of these fields, the system displays a data window that explains how the result was calculated and the data that was found to support it. The next section explains how the details in the data window are calculated.

If no record exists on the Academic Progress tab of SVAMSTD for the reporting term, the SS10 element is reported with the value N (No) and the SS11.4 element is reported with the value 0 (No).

If there is a single record for with a service code that is defined on SVVPRST with a probation support service of either Probation Support Intervention (A) or Support Pending Dismissal (C), the SS10 element is reported with the respective probation support service value (A or C). If there are no such records, the SS10 element is reported with the value N (No).

If one of the following conditions is true, the SS11.4 element is reported with the value 1 (Yes):
  • A record exists with a service code that is defined on SVVPRST with a probation support service of Other Academic Progress (OAP)
  • An extra second record exists that was not reported in SS10 with a service code that is defined on SVVPRST with a probation support service of either Probation Support Intervention (A) or Support Pending Dismissal (C)

If neither of these conditions is true, the SS11.4 element is reported with the value 0 (No)

Note: The system does not use the same record to report A or C for element SS10 and to report 1 for element SS11.4.

Student Credit for Prior Learning Report (SY)

The SY Student Credit for Prior Learning (SY) is a new term file. The file contains one record for each distinct combination of college, student, and assessment of credit for prior learning which occurred during the term.

Districts report information on student credit for prior learning assessed during the reporting term. One record is submitted for each combination of student and course for which a student was assessed for credit for prior learning during the reporting term.

Use the SVRCASY process to run the SY report. This report is not dependent on the REPT Engine (GVAREPT and GVPRMIS) used to run the existing MIS reports. Elements for the SY report are SY01, SY02, SY03, and SY04. (The element list is subject to change; check the CCCCO's data element dictionary (DED) for current values.)

The output file which is in .DAT format is used for final submission to CCCCO, and the file which is in .LIS format (user-friendly output) is used to evaluate results and troubleshoot errors/warnings in Banner as needed. After fixing the data issues, you can re-run the process to generate the .DAT file again before submitting to CCCCO.

The following criteria must be satisfied for a student's credit for prior learning to be reported in the SY report:

On the Transfer Course (SHATRNS) page—
  • The equivalent course detail block entered in SHATRNS is within the specified date range.
  • Campus entered in SHATRNS matches the District code entered by user, and the reporting term’s CB report contains Subject and Course.
On the Course Maintenance (SHATCKN) page—
  • The course, grade, person course attribute entered in SHATCKN is within the specified date range.
  • Campus entered in SHATCKN matches the District code entered by user, and the reporting term’s CB report contains Subject and Course.
  • Person Course Attribute is one of the attribute codes entered.
For more details on seed data for SY, see Student Credit for Prior Learning Report (SY) under the MIS mapping scripts and seed data section.
Parameter Name Required? Description Values
Start Date Yes The first day after the end of the previous term.  
End Date Yes The last date of the term being reported.  
District ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup. District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
Term Code Yes Term for which data is being reported. Term Code Validation Page (STVTERM)
Attribute(s) - credit by exam No Attribute(s) code for credit by exam.  
UTF8 to Ascii Yes Determines whether Ascii conversion is required for the data file.  

Student Vision Aligned Report (VR)

The Student Vision Aligned report (VR) is a term file. The file contains one record for each distinct combination of college, student, service program, and type of service which occurred during the term.

Districts report information on services provided during the reporting term. One record is submitted for each combination of student, service program, and type of service provided during the reporting term.

Use the SVRCAVR process to run the VR report.

This report is not dependent on the REPT Engine (GVAREPT and GVPRMIS) that is used to run the existing MIS reports. Elements for the VR report are VR01, VR02, and VR03. This element list is subject to change. Verify the list using the CCCCO data element dictionary (DED).

The output .DAT file is used for final submission to CCCCO. The user-friendly .LIS file is used to evaluate results and troubleshoot errors and warnings in Banner, as needed. After fixing any data issues, you can re-run the process to generate the .DAT file again before you submit to CCCCO.

At least one of the following criteria must be satisfied for services provided to a student to be reported in the VR report:

  1. Student has services reported on the MESA/ASEM tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VM program. The VM services are read with the SVVMSSA view.
  2. Student has services reported on the MCHS/ECHS tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VH program. The VH services are read with the SVVMCSS view.
  3. Student has services reported on the Foster Youth tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VN program. The VN services are read with the SVVMSSA view.
  4. Student has services reported on the College and Career Access Pathways tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VD program. The VD services are read with the SVVCCAP view.
  5. Student has services reported on the Work-based Learning tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VW program. The VN services are read with the SVVMSSA view. The VW services are read with the SVVSTWK view.
  6. Student has services reported on the AAHNPI tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VA program. The VA services are read with the SVVNHPI view.
  7. Student has services reported on the SEA tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VE program. The VE services are read with the SVVSEAP view.
  8. Student has services reported on the Transfer Center tab of SVAMIST. These services will be reported for the VT program. The VT services are read with the SVVTRCT view.
  9. Student has services reported on the Veterans tab of SVANEED. These services will be reported for the VR program.
  10. Student has eligible services reported on the Disability Services tab of SGADISA. These services will be reported for the SD program.
  11. Student has services reported on the Education Opportunity Programs and Services tab of SGAEOPS. These services will be reported for the SE program. The district code must be entered on SGAEOPS for the data to be reported. The SE services will be read with the SVVEOPS view.
  12. Student has services reported on the Other Educational Programs tab of SGAEOPS. These services will be reported for the VC program. The district code must be entered on SGAEOPS for the data to be reported. The VC services are read with the SVVCARE view.
  13. Student has services reported on the Student Data tab of SVACWSD. These services will be reported for the SC program. The SC services will be read with the SVVCALW view.
  14. Student has on campus or off campus child care hours reported on the Student Data tab of SVACWSD. These services will be reported for the SC program and the D06 service. These hours will be totaled before reporting. Any D06 service entered anywhere else will be flagged as an error and ignored.
  15. Student has work activities for status 1 or status 2 reported on the Student Data tab of SVACWSD. These services will be reported for the SC program and the D14 service. These hours will be totaled before reporting. Any D14 service entered anywhere else will be flagged as an error and ignored.
  16. Student has Direct Aid entries on TSAAREV that have been identified on SOAXREF as being for a program and service.
  17. Student has Financial Aid resources on RPAARSC that have been identified on SOAXREF as being for a program and service. The term code must be entered for the data to be reported.

For more details on seed data for VR, see Student Vision Aligned Report (VR) under the MIS mapping scripts and seed data section.

Parameter Name Required? Description Values
District ID Yes District/College ID assigned by the CCCCO (MIS element GI01). The GTVDICD value specifies the group of campus to be report based on the STVCAMP setup District/Division Code Validation (GTVDICD)
Term Code Yes Term for which data is being reported Term Code Validation Page (STVTERM)
UTF8 to ASCII Yes Determines whether ASCII conversion is required for the data file  

Common problems and possible solutions

  1. The student does not have the expected Financial Aid data.
    1. Verify that the term code on RPAARSC matches the term code for the report.
    2. Triple check the SOAXREF crosswalks for RTVARSC.
  2. The student does not have the expected Accounts Receivable data.
    1. Verify that the term code on TSAAREV matches the term code for the report.
    2. Triple check the SOAXREF crosswalks for TSADETC.
  3. The student does not have expected CARE data.

    Verify that the district code on SGAEOPS matches the district code for the report.

  4. The student does not have the expected EOPS data.

    Verify that the district code on SGAEOPS matches the district code for the report.

  5. The student has child care or work study hours that are not being reported.
    1. Verify that the data is on the SVACWSD page but is not in the services section.
    2. Any child care or work study hours that are required to be reported for any other program must be manually added to the report before it is submitted. This can change in a future release.
Student Vision Aligned Report (VR) design details

The MIS-VR report contains information about services that a student receives for a program; both the services and the programs are defined by the CCCCO. Every program can provide every service. Please refer to the CCCCO site for the current list of programs and services.

Details

Most of these program or service combinations are for counts (for example, how many times did the Veterans program provide academic counseling to a student during the term). However, a few services are to be reported as dollar amounts and a few other services are to be reported as hours of service provided. The CCCCO documentation will provide the current list.

For the two categories currently to be reported as dollar amounts, we are utilizing SOAXREF to identify both the program (the VR01 element) and the service (the VR02 element). Care must be taken to enter the crosswalks for these two elements. Banner will use Accounts Receivable data identified by the detail code (TSADETC) and the Financial Aid resource data identified by the resource code (RTVARSC).

For example, say that TSADETC code = T123 is for the service Direct Aid to Students – Textbooks (service code = D01) and will only be provided by the CARE program (program code = VC). You will need these two entries in SOAXREF for label = TSADETC.

EDI qualifier Electronic Value Banner Value Description
VR01<DICD> D0101 VC CARE program
VR02<DICD> D0101 T123 Direct Aid to Students - Textbooks

Note that a TSADETC code can only be mapped to one program code and one service code.

A similar crosswalk setup is needed for the Financial Aid resource code. The below example shows associated the ADRC1 resource code with the CalWorks program (program code = SC) and the Direct Aid to Students – Emergency Aid service (service code = D02).

EDI qualifier Electronic Value Banner Value Description
VR01<DICD> D0201 SC CalWorks program
VR02<DICD> D0201 ADRC1 Direct Aid to Students - Emergency Aid

An additional crosswalk mapping must be configured for the Disability Services resource code. All Disability Services reported will be associated with program code: SD. The specific service assigned to each student is stored in Student Disability Services (SGADISA) page. A new services block was not implemented for Disability Services, unlike other programs, because service-level details are already maintained using institution-specific service codes defined in Service Code Validation (STVSSER) page.

These service codes defined in STVSSER must be mapped to the corresponding MIS-VR values. This mapping is maintained in SOAXREF under the crosswalk label STVSSRC.

  • The electronic qualifier should be VR02<DICD>, where <DICD> is the district/college ID.
  • The electronic value should be Cxxyy:
    • Where xx is the service code as specified by the Chancellor's office.
    • Where yy is available to specify multiple Banner codes for the service.
  • The Banner value for this entry must correspond to your institution’s STVSSER code.

Example:

EDI qualifier Electronic Value Banner Value Description
VR02<DICD> C0101 ACAD This configuration maps the ACAD code to the C01 service, which represents Counseling – Academic.
VR02<DICD> C0102 MINO This configuration also maps the MINO code to the C01 service.
Note:

If a student has a SGADISA entry that is not cross walked on SOAXREF, that entry will be skipped without any message.

In the EDI Qualifier column, replace DICD with the District ID of the college.

Summary of Crosswalk Configuration Requirements

For each Student Account Receivable code to be reported:

  • Create two crosswalk entries in SOAXREF with the label TSADETC.
  • Both entries must share the same Electronic Value (for example, D0101).
  • VR01: Map the Banner value to the corresponding MIS-VR program code.
  • VR02: Map the Banner value to the detail code of your institution.

For each Financial Aid resource code to be reported:

  • Create two crosswalk entries in SOAXREF with the label RTVARSC.
  • Both entries must share the same Electronic Value (for example, D0201).
  • VR01: Map the Banner value to the corresponding MIS-VR program code.
  • VR02: Map the Banner value to the resource code of your institution.

For each Disability Service to be reported:

  • Create one crosswalk entry in SOAXREF with the label STVSSRC.
  • This entry must be VR02, mapping the Banner value to the service code of your institution.
